# dilla-web-2a — recover and badge: a second browser by recovery key, and a quiet client that badges and notifies Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Make the recovery key recover something and let one account span two browsers, and make the client show what happened while a person was not looking. After this plan: (A) a browser signs in to an existing account with the host login (password, plus TOTP when the account has it) and the recovery key, becomes a listed device of that account, and reads and sends in the account's channels; the sealed root and state objects live on the instance (`/v1/backups`); device registration is gated by a host-login assertion and the signed device list (C13); the instance verifies every published list, acts on a revocation, serves list history, and caps devices and enrolments per user; Settings → Devices lists the account's devices and offers "Sign out and revoke" and "forget this browser"; the schema moves from v1 to v2 by a real migration. (B) the client holds a group for every visible E2EE channel and DM of every community it is in (join-all at community load, paced for 200 groups), `groups()` no longer loads MLS state, DMs work through a null community from the core to the shell, every channel and DM carries unread and mention badges from a device-local read marker, and the page raises desktop notifications for DMs and mentions by default with Settings → Notifications to change it. web-2b (edits, deletes, reactions, pins, replies, mentions in the composer, attachments) and web-2c (leaf validation, safety numbers, search, remaining settings, diagnostics, tab hand-over, typing) follow and are out of this plan.

**Architecture:** Unchanged from web-1 (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-05-dilla-web-1.md`): one dedicated worker per tab owns the KEK, the encrypted OPFS store, the Rust core, the session token and the single gateway; Rust decides and persists, TypeScript transports, the page renders slices and sends commands. This plan adds to Rust the recovery-key paths (open the sealed objects, enrol a device by signing its credential and list v+1 with the reconstituted SSK, re-seal the state object, revoke), a persisted epoch and pending-commit per group so `groups()` is a query, DM groups with a null community, a read marker with unread and mention counts, and a settings table; to the facade the matching exports; to dillad the backup routes, assertion-gated registration inside establish, the device-list gate in `issue()`, verified device-list publication with the server's revocation action and a history read, and the per-user cap and rate; to client-core the enrolment flow, a load-free engine with join-all, DM groups, badges and a notices slice; to the page a sign-in ceremony, Settings → Devices and → Notifications, DM and badge rendering and the page-side notifier. Every new refusal is accompanied by the statement of who can trigger it against an honest party (lesson e), and every server behaviour a client relies on is also added to the TypeScript server model (`ModelDs`) and, where the e2e drives it, to the native testkit peer (lesson f).

**Tech Stack:** As web-1's: Rust 1.98.1, `dilla-core` on OpenMLS 0.9.0, `rusqlite` 0.40.2 (native SQLCipher; wasm `sqlite-wasm-rs` 0.5.5 with `sqlite3mc`, `sqlite-wasm-vfs` 0.2.0), `aes-gcm` 0.10.3, `hkdf` 0.13, `ed25519-dalek` 2.2, `zeroize` 1, wasm-bindgen 0.2.128 / wasm-pack 0.15.0 under `wasm-release`; Go 1.27.0 (`github.com/jonasthim/dilla`), sqlc v1.31.1; TypeScript 5.9.3, React 19.3.0, Vite 7, vitest 3, Storybook 9, ESLint 9.39.5 with typescript-eslint 8.71.1, jsx-a11y 6.10.2, react-hooks 7.1.1; Playwright 1.63.0 exact (Chromium 153 under `channel: 'chromium'`, Firefox 155, WebKit 26.6 in CI only); the Rust `dilla-testkit web-driver` as the native counterparty. No new dependency of any kind (pin table below).

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-23-dilla-design.md` (Identity L468–490, Clients L420–445 and L510–524, Error handling L600–637, Testing L637–653, the design section L166–330), `docs/design/brief.md` (the visual authority; brief:121–123 the CHANNELS / DMS tabs and the unread pills, :129–137 the status bar, :151–152 and :179–181 the settings sections named here, :233 the recovery-key entry), the brief's accessibility floor (brief:7 and the spec's design section L166–330; there is no separate accessibility document in `docs/design/`), and the normative `protocol/02-delivery-service.md`, `03-identity.md`, `06-backup-archive.md`, `09-http-api.md`, each amended by the tasks named in "Protocol and spec edits in this plan" with a `07-versioning.md` row. Authorities in order: `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-06-dilla-web-2/facts/rulings.md` (the three plans; Q01–Q14 provisional founder rulings; Q15–Q30 controller rulings), `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-05-dilla-web/facts/rulings.md` (C1–C24, F1–F18 still bind), the web-1 plan's Global Constraints and Interface ledger and its Follow-up cards, the web-1 ledger `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-05-dilla-web-1/progress.md`; then `facts/interfaces.md` and `facts/deviations.md` of this wave, the critic, the gap files G1–G8 and the six lens files; then the spec and the code. Where a facts file and the code disagree, **the code wins** and the task says so; this head records every such case it met in "Rulings made by the architect".

**Never written:** everything web-1 forbids (its Global Constraints line 78: Go MLS code; cgo; an ORM; a router library; a `dillad serve` flag or config key that exists for tests; CORS or `OPTIONS`; COOP/COEP; a gateway `resume` frame; `PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL`; a second `DillaStorage` or a long-lived `ConnHandle` clone; MLS, TLS or credential parsing in TypeScript; a key, token, KEK, **recovery key, enrolment assertion** or **host password** in `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, a cookie, a URL, a log line, a slice or a `postMessage` to anything but the owning page — the recovery key crosses page → worker exactly once per entry, inside one command, and is zeroised in Rust; the assertion and the password live in worker memory only, for one command's duration; `innerHTML`; inline `<script>`/`<style>`; `eval`; a `data:` or `blob:` worker; any new runtime dependency). Also never: a `Notification` built in the worker (Q30: the page builds them); a notification icon other than none (`img-src 'self'` stays; the CSP is widened only in web-2b); a change to the served Content-Security-Policy; a change to `core/dilla-core-wasi` or the wasi ABI; a server migration (every table this plan needs exists); `protocol/04` or `protocol/08` edits (web-2b, web-2c).

**Licence and file headers (F14)** — as web-1: `@dilla/client-core` and `@dilla/web` AGPL-3.0-or-later, `@dilla/core-wasm` Apache-2.0, new Rust modules in the Apache-2.0 crates, Go in the AGPL module; no SPDX or licence header in any file (the repository has none); Rust and Go files open with the module doc comment that says what the file is for.

**Copy rules (F10) and the lint that enforces them**
- The words `scripts/check-ui-copy.mjs` forbids (`kanal(s)`, `team(s)`, `PMs`, `E2E(E)`, `end-to-end`, `encrypted`, `encryption`, `SRTP`, `X3DH`, `Signal Protocol`, `SQLCipher`, `AES-NNN`, `MLS`) appear in no string literal and no JSX text of `packages/ui/src`, `packages/web/src` or `packages/client-core/src`, tests and stories included. **This plan adds no surface that F10 allow-lists** (Settings → Privacy is web-2c), so `packages/web/src/strings/privacy.ts` is still not created and the lint is not touched.
- Every user-visible string lives in `packages/web/src/strings/en.ts` and is passed to `@dilla/ui` as props; `@dilla/ui` components added here hard-code no English except overridable `aria-label` defaults. Casing (Q14, ruling 26 of web-1): lower-case labels in the chrome (the rail, channel list, DMs tab, badges, status bar, settings navigation labels and row labels), sentence case on ceremony, splash and dialog surfaces (sign-in steps, the revoke dialog, the forget dialog, Settings section headings and body text). No exclamation marks; no "secure", "safe", "protected"; no lock glyph.
- No string promises what web-2a cannot do: the second browser sees messages from its join on (no archive), pins are not kept across browsers, and the recovery key does not reach other devices; L-COPY-02 carries the exact sentences, including the two web-1 strings that change now that recovery exists (`onboarding.keys.loss`, `onboarding.browser.oneBrowser`; web-1 ruling 27).
- A client never switches on a server `detail` text: every mapping from a refusal to a string is by `code` and `status`. `packages/web/src/copy.test.ts`'s detail-switch grep stays green and gains the forms card 53 lists (`switch (…detail)`, `.test(…detail)`, `.indexOf(`, `.search(`, `.toLowerCase() ===`) in task 18.
- Exact strings are fixed once in **L-COPY-02**; `docs/design/flows/03-sign-in.md` (task 15), the stories (tasks 16–17), `en.ts` (tasks 18–20) and the e2e (tasks 21–22) quote it and none changes a key or a text.

**Accessibility rules (WCAG 2.2 AA)** — as web-1 (tokens only; three themes and reduced motion; a story per state; `vitest-axe`; the Storybook test-runner's axe gate incl. `target-size` for the story groups `Form/`, `Ceremony/`, `Shell/`, `Conversation/` and the new `Settings/`; 24×24 CSS px targets; `aria-disabled` not `disabled` for blocked controls; forms as `<form noValidate>` with a `type="submit"` forward button; paste allowed in every field, the recovery-key field included, F2). Additions fixed here:
- Keyboard map. The web-1 shell order (skip link → rail → channel list → header → log → composer → status bar) stays; the sidebar gains a `tablist` (channels / DMs) **before** the list as one tab stop with `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight` between the two tabs; the rail's last item is the settings button (inside the roving group, after "join a server"). Settings is a route-driven modal dialog (`SettingsFrame`, L-UI-24): focus moves to its `<h1>` on open; its navigation is one tab stop with roving focus (`ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown`, `Home`/`End`); `Escape` closes it and returns to the route the person came from and to the rail's settings button. No single-character shortcut (2.1.4), and no new modifier shortcut in this plan (Q14 names ⌘/Ctrl+K and Ctrl+/ for web-2c).
- Badges: a `Pill` inside a `ChannelRow` or rail item is decorative for assistive technology; the row's accessible name carries the count in words through `aria-label` (`shell.channels.rowLabel`, L-COPY-02), and a muted row says so.
- Notifications are never the only signal: every event that may notify also badges.
- The sign-in ceremony follows flow 01's rules: focus to the step `<h1>` on step change, first field in error on a failed submit, errors as text bound with `aria-describedby` inside `role="alert"`, busy buttons `aria-disabled` with the pressed button keeping focus.
- F16 artefacts: tasks 16, 17, 18, 19, 20 run `packages/ui/scripts/shoot-stories.mjs` and leave PNGs of every new story in all three themes under `target/ui-screens/web-2a/`; the supervisor attaches them to the review, and task 23 makes the `ui` job upload them.

**Testing**
- TDD in every implementation task: the failing test first, its recorded failure, the implementation, the passing run, one commit.
- **A test must be able to fail (lesson a).** For each security- or correctness-critical assertion the task names the mutation that turns it red and has one step that applies it, shows the red run, and reverts it. The task index names the mutation.
- **Every new refusal states its attacker (lesson e).** A task that adds a refusal writes, next to the test, who can trigger it against an honest party and why they cannot. The ledger entries below carry the statement for each refusal this plan adds.
- **The model answers what the server answers (lesson f).** A server behaviour a TypeScript task relies on is added to `ModelDs` in the task that first relies on it (task 10 lists them), and to the native peer where the e2e drives it (task 9).
- **The migration is tested on a v1 store (lesson g).** Task 1 commits a v1 fixture store and opens it.
- The module-wide Go command is pinned and never narrowed in a task's final verification: `/home/thim/.local/go/bin/go -C /home/thim/Repositories/dilla/.claude/worktrees/sdd-dilla-protocol test -race -shuffle=on -timeout 15m ./...`. A Go test that cannot run under the race detector is listed in `NON_RACE_STEP` of `scripts/check-ci-workflow.mjs` and in the `go` job's non-race step in the same task (none is expected).
- Rust final verification mirrors `rust-native` and `rust-wasm-node`: `/home/thim/.cargo/bin/cargo fmt --manifest-path /home/thim/Repositories/dilla/.claude/worktrees/sdd-dilla-protocol/Cargo.toml --all --check`, `/home/thim/.cargo/bin/cargo clippy --manifest-path /home/thim/Repositories/dilla/.claude/worktrees/sdd-dilla-protocol/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings`, `/home/thim/.cargo/bin/cargo test --manifest-path /home/thim/Repositories/dilla/.claude/worktrees/sdd-dilla-protocol/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked`; for every task that touches `core/` also `/home/thim/.cargo/bin/cargo test --manifest-path /home/thim/Repositories/dilla/.claude/worktrees/sdd-dilla-protocol/Cargo.toml -p dilla-core --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --locked --features vectors`, `/home/thim/.cargo/bin/cargo test --manifest-path /home/thim/Repositories/dilla/.claude/worktrees/sdd-dilla-protocol/Cargo.toml -p dilla-core-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --locked` and `/home/thim/.cargo/bin/cargo clippy --manifest-path /home/thim/Repositories/dilla/.claude/worktrees/sdd-dilla-protocol/Cargo.toml -p dilla-core-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --lib --locked -- -D warnings`.
- TypeScript final verification: `npm --prefix /home/thim/Repositories/dilla/.claude/worktrees/sdd-dilla-protocol test`. Unit tests of `@dilla/client-core` and `@dilla/web` never load the wasm: `FakeCore` (account half) and `ModelCore` with `ModelDs` (group half) stand in; the parity fixture L-CORE-10 stays at eight cases and both `8` assertions stay (no `group_apply` result shape changes in this plan).
- **Browser thresholds (lesson c).** The CI runner has 4 vCPUs and is 3–5× slower than the dev machine: a browser test waits for a state, never a duration; every wait has an explicit timeout ≥ 30 s locally / 90 s in CI; no assertion is an upper bound on elapsed time; `workers: 1`, `retries: 0`. The join-all proof asserts the mechanism (every expected group reaches state 2; the open channel was not blocked), not a time. Task 13 measures; task 23 budgets from the measurement.
- **Every browser test closes what it opens (lesson d).** A second browser context (task 21) is opened through a fixture that closes it in `finally`; the web-driver children are closed; the pattern is `e2e/web/support/persistent.ts` and `e2e/web/support/app.ts`.
- CI is fail-closed: no `|| true`, no `continue-on-error`, no `if: always()` on a gate step; every `upload-artifact` sets `if-no-files-found: error`.

**Execution environment**
- The implementer (Codex under a supervisor) works in a sandbox that has network access and can launch Chromium and Firefox. It cannot write the git directory: **the supervisor makes every commit.** The supervisor re-runs every Firefox leg itself before committing.
- `TMPDIR` is `/home/thim/Repositories/dilla/.claude/worktrees/sdd-dilla-protocol/.superpowers/tmp`. That path is too long for Chromium's socket files, so browser profile directories are never under it: persistent Playwright contexts use `/tmp/dw/<project>-<worker>` (and the second browser of task 21 `/tmp/dw/<project>-<worker>-b`), created and removed by the fixture; the test host's data directory is `/tmp/dw/host-<port>`.
- Fixed ports, one owner each. Existing: 5178, 6006, 8443/8444, 5179, 7880/7882, 8453/8454 (core-worker suite and the spike of task 13), 8463/8464 (web suite), 6016–6019 (web-1 screenshot runs). New: **6020** (task 16), **6021** (task 17), **6022** (task 18), **6023** (task 19), **6024** (task 20), each the screenshot script's static server for that task only. Go tests bind port 0. 5432 is opened only by the optional Postgres container.
- WebKit cannot launch on the dev host; it is gated in CI only (`webkit-web` keeps its two web-1 specs; this plan adds none to it: Q30 marks notifications untestable on WebKit, and enrolment runs on Chromium and Firefox).
- **A wiped store needs a page reload.** `CoreHandle.close()` keeps the OPFS access handles and `pause()` releases them, but `sqlite-wasm-vfs` 0.2.0's `install` returns the already registered pool, so a worker that wiped its store cannot open a fresh one (`sahpool.rs:964-971`). Every wipe (`signOutRevoke`, `forgetBrowser`, `E_LIST_RACE`) therefore ends in the `cleared` phase (L-TS-23), which accepts no command, and the page answers `cleared` with `window.location.replace(…)` (L-TS-27). No task works around this in the worker.

**CI rules**
- No new job, with one exception: L-CI-11's split of `browser-web` into `browser-web-core` and `browser-web` when the measured budget passes 45 minutes (the split adds the new name to `REQUIRED_JOBS` and the `needs` rule in the same task). Every change to a job's steps (the `ui` screenshot line and its artifact, the `browser-web` budget) is made in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and in `REQUIRED_STEPS` of `scripts/check-ci-workflow.mjs` in the same task (23), with a case in `scripts/check-ci-workflow.test.mjs` that removes the step and expects the checker to fail.
- Race-gated Go tests are listed in the non-race step (none expected).

**Protocol-edit rules**
- Every edit to a `protocol/*.md` document gets its `protocol/07-versioning.md` change-table row in the same task and commit, appended as the last row in the table's form (`| date | e2ee 1, media 1, wire 1 | **Behaviour change.** … |` or `**Additive.** …`), and is listed in "Protocol and spec edits in this plan". No version axis is bumped: no client has shipped (07 precedent), and every edit here is additive or documents behaviour of this build.
- 07 step 4 (the founder's approval and a recorded independent review) is recorded as provisional on the rulings of `facts/rulings.md`, as for F1–F18.
- `npm run check:docs` stays green after every protocol edit.

**Commits**
- One commit per task, conventional subject (`feat(core): …`, `feat(wasm): …`, `feat(store): …`, `feat(api): …`, `feat(client-core): …`, `feat(ui): …`, `feat(web): …`, `feat(testkit): …`, `test(e2e): …`, `ci: …`, `docs(design): …`, `docs(protocol): …`), made by the supervisor in one command line: `git -C /home/thim/Repositories/dilla/.claude/worktrees/sdd-dilla-protocol commit -s -m "<subject>" -m "<body>" --trailer "Co-Authored-By: Codex <noreply@openai.com>" --trailer "Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01XLFud8eoDaqf8uiZq5wjuP"`. The final paragraph of every commit message is therefore the two trailer lines `Co-Authored-By: Codex <noreply@openai.com>` and `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01XLFud8eoDaqf8uiZq5wjuP` followed by the `Signed-off-by` that `-s` adds. A `-m` value never spans two lines, and the trailers are never passed as `-m` paragraphs.
- Task 23 may end in more than one commit: a red first CI run is fixed by further commits inside the task; the workflow runs on `pull_request`, so task 23 opens the plan's PR as a draft when it does not exist yet, and the green run's id goes into the PR description and `progress.md`.

## Interface ledger

The single source of truth for every interface that crosses a task boundary. A task text may add private helpers; it may not change a name, a type, a field order, a constant or an error code written here. If a drafter finds the code makes an entry impossible, the task says so in a "Ledger conflict" note at its top and the reviewer rules; the drafter does not silently adapt. Every interface the web-1 ledger fixed keeps its web-1 id and is cited, not restated, unless it changes here (then the change is stated under a new id with the web-1 id named).

Conventions as web-1 (`b16`, `b32`, `b64`, `uint`, `tstr`, `x|null`; one deterministic CBOR item per boundary value; `_body` is the exact HTTP request body; "the 200 body of …" is the response bytes as received; timestamps are unix seconds).

### L-CORE — `dilla-core` (`src/client`)

**L-CORE-20 app schema v2 and `migrate_app`** (`src/client/schema.rs`; Q23; amends web-1 L-SQL-10)

The v2 shape (what a fresh store gets, and what a v1 store becomes):

```sql
-- L-SQL-20: app_groups gains two columns, app_messages one, two tables are new; everything else is L-SQL-10 verbatim.
ALTER TABLE app_groups   ADD COLUMN epoch          INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0;   -- the MLS epoch of the stored group, written whenever it changes
ALTER TABLE app_groups   ADD COLUMN pending_commit INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0;   -- 1 while this device holds an unmerged commit it built
ALTER TABLE app_messages ADD COLUMN mention        INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0;   -- 1 when a status-0 type-0 row from another device mentions this user (L-CORE-24)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS app_read_state (
  group_id      BLOB    PRIMARY KEY CHECK (length(group_id) = 16),
  last_read_seq INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  last_read_at  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
) WITHOUT ROWID;
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS app_settings (k TEXT PRIMARY KEY, v TEXT NOT NULL) WITHOUT ROWID;
```

`APP_SCHEMA` (the fresh-store batch) creates every table with the v2 columns inline (`epoch`, `pending_commit` after `max_epoch`; `mention` after `franking_tag`) and seeds `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO app_meta (k, v) VALUES ('schema', x'02')`. `MIGRATE_V1_TO_V2` is the batch above (the three `ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN` lines carry no `CHECK`; Rust enforces 0|1) followed by `UPDATE app_meta SET v = x'02' WHERE k = 'schema'`. The body lives in a connection-level `fn migrate_conn(c: &Connection) -> Result<u64, StorageError>` (private to `schema.rs`'s crate): runs `APP_SCHEMA`, reads `schema`, and when it is `1` runs `MIGRATE_V1_TO_V2` on the same connection and returns `1`; it returns the value it found (`1` or `2`; a fresh store reads `2`); a value above 2 is returned unchanged. `pub fn migrate_app(storage: &DillaStorage) -> Result<u64, StorageError>` is one unit around `migrate_conn` (the public surface; the tests call it). `ClientCore::open` refuses a value above 2 with `E_CORE_STATE` "app schema <n> is newer than this build". New `app_meta` key: `enrol` (L-CORE-22). `ClientCore::open` does **not** call `migrate_app`: `DillaStorage::unit` does not nest (`src/mls/tx.rs:146-152`), so `open` runs `migrate_conn` and, when it returned `1`, the **backfill** inside **one** unit (a failed backfill rolls the `ALTER TABLE`s back, which task 1 tests), before loading the DSK: for every `app_groups` row with `state IN (0, 1, 2, 3)`, `DillaGroup::load`; found → `UPDATE app_groups SET epoch = ?, pending_commit = ?` from `epoch()` and `has_pending_commit()`; not found → the row keeps `0, 0`; for every `app_messages` row with `status = 0 AND type = 0 AND sender_user <> own user` (by user, ruling 29) whose `body` satisfies `mentions_me` (L-CORE-24) → `mention = 1`; and the `identity` record is rewritten from v1 to v2 (L-CORE-22). The backfill runs once: after it `schema` is `2` and a later `open` finds `2`. **Attacker statement:** the migration refuses nothing new; a store whose MLS group fails to load keeps `epoch 0`, which `take_group` already turns into `E_CORE_STATE` "the stored group does not match its row" on first use (L-CORE-07 "Loaded groups"), so a corrupt row is visible, not silent.

**L-CORE-21 `groups()` is a query; `group_row`** (`src/client/groups.rs`; Q29; amends web-1 L-CORE-07's `groups()` text, same wire shape)

```rust
/// [[group_id b16, kind uint, community_id b16|null, target_id b16, state uint, epoch uint,
///   next_seq uint, proposals_pending uint, pending_commit uint 0|1]] ordered by group_id —
/// epoch and pending_commit are app_groups.epoch and app_groups.pending_commit; no MLS state is loaded.
pub fn groups(&self) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ClientError>;
/// CBOR null for an unknown id, else the one row of groups() for it (the same 9 elements).
pub fn group_row(&self, group_id: &[u8; 16]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ClientError>;
```

Writers (each inside the unit of the operation that changes the value; `epoch` is read from the `DillaGroup` right after the change): `group_create` leaves the defaults (0, 0); `group_join_external` sets **`epoch` to the joined group's epoch** and `pending_commit = 0` on the row it updates or inserts (OpenMLS 0.9.0's `join_by_external_commit` merges the external commit before it returns, `external_commits.rs:371-413`, so a state-1 row's group is already at e + 1; `max_epoch` is still raised only by `group_joined`); `group_joined` sets `epoch` to the joined group's epoch; `welcomes_apply` sets `epoch` to the joined epoch and `pending_commit = 0` (UPDATE or INSERT); `group_apply` sets `epoch` after every merge (staged, own pending) and `pending_commit = 0` whenever it merges or clears a pending commit, and on self-removal sets `epoch = 0, pending_commit = 0` with `state = 4`; `commit_build` sets `pending_commit = 1` after the commit is built; `commit_confirm` sets `epoch` after the merge and `pending_commit = 0`; `commit_abort` sets `pending_commit = 0`; `group_discard` deletes the row (and its `app_read_state` row) or, returning it to state 3 or 4, sets **`epoch = 0, pending_commit = 0` in both cases** (a discarded resync has no MLS group left: `groups.rs:295-297`, `:395-397`; `tests/client_groups.rs:359-364` and `tests/client_hardening.rs:1226` pin `epoch == 0` for that row). `cursor_body` reads `app_groups.epoch` instead of loading the group; one corner changes: a state-3 row with no stored group (after a discarded resync) answers `[next_seq − 1, 0]` where web-1 answered `E_CORE_STATE "group state 3"` — no test pins the old answer and dillad's cursor endpoint does not compare the epoch (`internal/ds/message.go:205-240`). The invariant every native test of task 1 asserts after each step of its scenarios: for every row in state 0–3, `groups()`'s `epoch` equals `DillaGroup::load(...).epoch()` and its `pending_commit` equals `has_pending_commit()`; for state 4, and for a state-3 row whose group was deleted, both are 0. **Mutation named:** remove the `epoch` write from `commit_confirm` → the invariant test goes red after the first confirmed commit.

**L-CORE-22 the identity record v2, the enrol record and phase 3** (`src/client/identity.rs`; amends web-1 L-CORE-06's record table)

- `identity` = `[2, instance_id b16, user_id b16, device_id b16, dsk_pub b32, umk_pub b32, ssk_pub b32, username tstr, credential bstr, device_list_body bstr, list_published uint 0|1, device_list bstr, state_uploaded uint 0|1]` — thirteen elements. `device_list` is the newest signed list (the 6-element CBOR of protocol/03) that the instance **accepted** (v1 at signup; promoted from the candidate by `device_list_published`; replaced by `own_device_list_update`). `device_list_body` is the PUT body of the **candidate** list (the newest this device built); `list_published` says whether the instance accepted it. The v1→v2 rewrite (L-CORE-20's backfill) sets `device_list` = element 1 (`blob`) of the decoded v1 `device_list_body`, and `state_uploaded = 0`.
- `enrol` = `[1, instance_id b16, device_id b16, dsk_pub b32, user_id b16|null]`. Present exactly in phase 3. `enrol` together with `identity` or `signup` is `E_CORE_STATE` "enrol record beside another phase".
- `Phase` gains `Enrolling(EnrolRecord)` (`EnrolRecord { instance_id: [u8; 16], device_id: [u8; 16], dsk_pub: [u8; 32], user_id: Option<[u8; 16]> }` with `encode`/`decode`); `identity()` (web-1 L-CORE-06, same 6-element shape) answers `[3, instance_id, user_id|null, device_id, "", 0]` in phase 3 (the enrol record carries no username: after a reload mid-ceremony the worker completes with `""` and `enterReady` reads the name from `GET /v1/accounts/me` for the `account` slice; the core keeps `""`). `session_sign` (purpose 0 or 1) and `session_store` accept phase 3, reading `instance_id`/`device_id` from the enrol record; `session`, `session_clear`, `sealed_objects`, `unload`, `settings`, `setting_put`, `setting_delete` answer in every phase; every other web-1 method, and `mark_read`/`activity` (they need the own device), answer `E_CORE_NO_IDENTITY` in phase 3 as in phase 1; `signup_submit`/`signup_complete`/`signup_reset` answer `E_CORE_STATE` "no signup is pending" and `signup_begin` answers `E_CORE_STATE` "an enrolment is pending". The split of ownership: task 1 lands the record types, the `Phase` variant, every `match` arm the variant forces, `identity()`'s phase-3 answer, `open`'s phase-3 DSK load and the v2 `IdentityRecord` (`signup_complete` writes `device_list` = the v1 blob, `state_uploaded = false`); task 3 lands every new method, `session_sign`/`session_store`'s phase-3 arms, `sealed_objects`' third element and `device_list_published`'s promotion.
- `sealed_objects()` (amends web-1 L-CORE-06) → `[root_sealed bstr|null, state_sealed bstr|null, state_uploaded uint 0|1]`; `state_uploaded` is 0 outside phase 2.
- `open` in phase 3 loads the DSK of the enrol record (`SignatureKeyPair::read` of its `dsk_pub`), as for the other phases.

**L-CORE-23 DM groups: a null community** (`src/client/{groups,wire}.rs`; Q25; amends web-1 L-CORE-07's three signatures)

```rust
pub fn group_create(&mut self, group_id: &[u8; 16], community_id: Option<&[u8; 16]>, channel_id: &[u8; 16],
    policy_version: u64, external_sender_pub: &[u8; 32]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ClientError>;
pub fn group_join_external(&mut self, group_id: &[u8; 16], community_id: Option<&[u8; 16]>, channel_id: &[u8; 16],
    policy_version: u64, info_body: &[u8], tree_body: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ClientError>;
/// `expected`: [[group_id b16, community_id b16|null, channel_id b16, policy_version uint]]
pub fn welcomes_apply(&mut self, welcomes_body: &[u8], expected: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ClientError>;
```

`binding` builds `DillaBinding { community_id: community.map(CommunityId::from_bytes), target_id: channel_id, kind: GroupKind::Text, … }` (a DM's text group is a `text` group with `community_id = null` and `target_id = channel_id`, protocol/09:394-396); `GroupRow::bound_to(community: Option<&[u8;16]>, channel)` compares `community_id` as an `Option` (`None` matches only a NULL column); `app_groups.community_id` is NULL for a DM row; `take_group`'s row check already compares `Option`s and does not change; the holder rule ("no other non-gone row holds the channel") is unchanged, keyed on `(target_id, kind)`. Every web-1 refusal text stays. The web-1 ledger's `ExpectedGroup.communityId: Id` becomes `Id | null` (L-TS-20). **Attacker statement:** a null community refuses nothing new; a Welcome whose binding carries a community for a channel the client expects as a DM (or the reverse) is already outcome 2 `E_BINDING` under L-CORE-07's binding comparison.

**L-CORE-24 read markers, mentions and activity** (`src/client/messages.rs`; Q09, Q29; spec:512 "on-device")

```rust
/// true when `body` contains "<@" + the 32 lower-case hex characters of `user_id` + ">", or "<@everyone>",
/// or "<@here>" — the readable mention syntax of protocol/09 (`<@(everyone|here|[0-9a-f]{32})>`), matched
/// literally (no regex, no case folding; upper-case hex does not match).
pub fn mentions_me(body: &str, user_id: &[u8; 16]) -> bool;

/// Any state but 4 (E_CORE_STATE "group state 4"); E_CORE_NOT_FOUND for an unknown group.
/// last_read_seq := max(last_read_seq, min(seq, next_seq - 1)); last_read_at := now. Never lowered.
pub fn mark_read(&mut self, group_id: &[u8; 16], seq: u64, now: u64) -> Result<(), ClientError>;

/// [[group_id b16, unread uint, mentions uint, last_seq uint, last_ts uint, last_read_seq uint]]
/// for every app_groups row in state 2 or 3, ordered by group_id. unread = COUNT of app_messages rows of the
/// group with status = 0 AND type = 0 AND sender_user <> own user AND seq > last_read_seq (a missing
/// app_read_state row counts as last_read_seq 0; a status-0 row always carries sender_user); mentions = the
/// same with mention = 1; last_seq and last_ts are the seq and recv_ts of the highest such row (0, 0 when
/// unread = 0). Phase 2 only (E_CORE_NO_IDENTITY otherwise), as mark_read.
pub fn activity(&self) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ClientError>;
```

The exclusion is by **user**, not device (ruling 29): with two browsers on one account, the person's own words typed in browser B must not badge or notify browser A. `insert_message` (web-1 `messages.rs:42`) takes `mention: bool`; `group_apply` passes `mentions_me(&body, &own.user_id) && sender_user != own.user_id` for a status-0 type-0 row and `false` for every other row; `send_confirm` passes `false`. The TypeScript `ModelCore` mirrors `markRead` and `activity` exactly (task 10), and the worker's notice filter (L-TS-24) uses the same rule. **Mutation named:** drop `sender_user <> own user` from `unread` → the activity test with an own confirmed message **and** with a message from the own user's other device goes red (the test holds both rows: an own-device row and a row whose `sender_user` is the own user but whose `sender_device` is another id).

**L-CORE-25 settings** (`src/client/settings.rs`; Q24)

```rust
pub fn settings(&self) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ClientError>;                    // [[k tstr, v tstr]] ordered by k
pub fn setting_put(&mut self, k: &str, v: &str) -> Result<(), ClientError>; // k 1..=128 bytes, v 0..=1024 bytes, else E_CORE_INPUT; upsert
pub fn setting_delete(&mut self, k: &str) -> Result<(), ClientError>;       // no-op when absent
```

Every phase answers (settings are device-local and survive `enrol_reset`; `resetDevice` wipes the store and with it the table).

**L-CORE-26 enrolment by recovery key, revocation, the own list** (`src/client/identity.rs`; F1, F2, F3, C13, Q03, Q08, Q13, Q26, Q27; protocol/03:234-238, 06:11-40)

```rust
/// Phase 0 only → phase 3. Generates the DSK (SignatureKeyPair::new, stored in OpenMLS's signature-key
/// table, C6) and a random 16-byte device_id; writes `enrol` = [1, instance_id, device_id, dsk_pub, null].
/// Returns [device_id b16, dsk_pub b32].
pub fn enrol_begin(&mut self, instance_id: &[u8; 16]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ClientError>;

/// Phase 3 only. The POST /v1/devices/{device_id}/sessions body of L-HTTP-54:
/// [nonce b32, 0, sig b64, [device_id b16, dsk_pub b32, 1, 1, placeholder bstr], login bstr]
/// sig = Ed25519(DSK, session_preimage(instance_id, device_id, nonce, 0)); login = the assertion's UTF-8
/// bytes, 1..=256 bytes (E_CORE_INPUT otherwise); placeholder = the 10-element CredentialIdentity with
/// v 1, umk_pub 32 zero bytes, user_id 16 zero bytes, this device_id, kind 0, tier 1, signer_tier 1,
/// ssk_pub 32 zero bytes and both signatures 64 zero bytes (the instance stores and never reads it;
/// the signed credential enters groups through KeyPackages).
pub fn enrol_session_sign(&self, nonce: &[u8; 32], login: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ClientError>;

/// Phase 3 only. Records the user id the pending session named (element 2 of the 201 body).
/// E_CORE_INPUT when all zero; E_CORE_STATE "user already recorded" when the record holds another id.
pub fn enrol_registered(&mut self, user_id: &[u8; 16]) -> Result<(), ClientError>;

/// Phase 3 with a recorded user_id only (E_CORE_STATE "no user recorded" otherwise). Everything below
/// runs in one unit, each refusal writing nothing, in this order:
///  1. rk = recovery_key_from_base32(recovery_key_normalise(recovery_key)) — a failure is E_RECOVERY_KEY.
///  2. root = open(k_header(rk), aad "dilla root v1", root_sealed): root_sealed must decode as
///     [1, nonce b12, ct bstr]; a decode failure is E_CORE_INPUT "root_sealed is malformed"; an AEAD
///     failure is E_RECOVERY_KEY; the plaintext must decode as [1, umk_priv b32, ssk_priv b32], else
///     E_CORE_INPUT "root object is malformed". umk_pub, ssk_pub derive from the two seeds.
///  3. pins: when state_sealed is empty (0 bytes: the instance holds no state object), or does not decode
///     as [1, nonce b12, ct bstr], or does not open under k_backup(rk) with aad "dilla state v1", or its
///     plaintext does not decode as [1, device_list bstr, pins array], then pins = the empty CBOR array
///     (0x80) and the method PROCEEDS (no refusal: the key is right, step 2 passed, and the served
///     SSK-verified list is the base; the re-seal of step 8 writes a sound object the caller uploads,
///     repairing the instance's copy). Otherwise `pins` is the object's pins as raw CBOR bytes, carried
///     through unchanged (Q08: the merge is the identity until pins exist on browsers, web-2c).
///  4. served = decode(list_body) as [version uint, blob bstr, ssk_signature b64, prev_hash b32] (the 200
///     body of GET /v1/users/{id}/device-list), E_CORE_INPUT "list_body is malformed"; list =
///     DeviceList::decode(blob) and list.verify(ssk_pub) must pass, else E_CREDENTIAL; list.unsigned.user_id
///     must equal the recorded user_id, else E_CREDENTIAL; list.unsigned.version must equal `version`,
///     the blob's prev_hash equal `prev_hash` and the blob's signature equal `ssk_signature` (all three outer
///     elements, as L-HTTP-55 checks on PUT), else E_CORE_INPUT "list_body elements disagree". The state
///     object's own list (step 3) is not compared: the served list is the base.
///  5. Already listed: if `list` names this device_id unrevoked with this dsk_pub, E_CORE_STATE "device is
///     listed" (an enrolment that was already completed; the caller re-establishes).
///  6. The credential: CredentialIdentity { v 1, umk_pub, user_id, device_id, kind User, tier Browser,
///     signer_tier Browser, ssk_pub, sig_umk_ssk = UmkSigner(umk_priv).sign_ssk(ssk_pub),
///     sig_ssk_dev = SskSigner(ssk_priv).sign_device(device_id, dsk_pub, User, Browser, Browser) };
///     verify_signatures(dsk_pub) must pass (E_CORE_STATE "credential does not verify" — a bug, not input).
///  7. next = DeviceListUnsigned { v 1, user_id, version: list.version + 1, prev_hash: list.hash(),
///     entries: list.entries ++ [DeviceEntry { device_id, dsk_pub, tier Browser, added_at now, revoked_at None }] },
///     signed by SskSigner(ssk_priv); next.verify(ssk_pub) must pass.
///  8. state' = seal(k_backup(rk), aad "dilla state v1", [1, next.encode(), pins]).
///  9. Writes: identity (L-CORE-22) with username, credential, device_list_body = PUT body of `next`,
///     list_published 0, device_list = list.encode() (the served, accepted list), state_uploaded 0;
///     state_sealed := state'; root_sealed := root_sealed as given; deletes `enrol`.
/// 10. umk_priv, ssk_priv, rk, k_header, k_backup and the root plaintext are Zeroizing and dropped here.
/// Returns [device_list_put_body bstr, state_sealed bstr]. Phase becomes 2.
pub fn enrol_complete(&mut self, recovery_key: &str, root_sealed: &[u8], state_sealed: &[u8], list_body: &[u8],
    username: &str, now: u64) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ClientError>;

/// Phase 3 only: deletes `enrol`, the DSK and any `session` record. Phase becomes 0.
pub fn enrol_reset(&mut self) -> Result<(), ClientError>;

/// Phase 2 only. Steps 1–4 of enrol_complete with the stored user_id (the served list's user_id must equal
/// it; the root's umk_pub/ssk_pub must equal the identity record's, else E_CREDENTIAL ""; step 3's tolerance
/// of a missing or unopenable state object applies here too). `device_ids` is 1..=64 ids, 16 bytes each,
/// concatenated (E_CORE_INPUT "device_ids must be 1..=64 ids of 16 bytes" otherwise; a repeated id is
/// E_CORE_INPUT "device_ids repeats an id"); every id must be an unrevoked entry of the served list
/// (E_CORE_NOT_FOUND "device is not an unrevoked entry of the list" otherwise). next = the served list with
/// revoked_at = now on those entries, version + 1, prev_hash = list.hash(), signed by the SSK and verified;
/// state' re-sealed with the state object's pins (or [] per step 3) unchanged. Writes device_list_body = PUT body of next, list_published 0,
/// device_list = the served list, state_uploaded 0, state_sealed := state'. Returns
/// [device_list_put_body bstr, state_sealed bstr]. Revoking this device is allowed (Q13); the caller then
/// wipes the store.
pub fn device_list_revoke(&mut self, recovery_key: &str, root_sealed: &[u8], state_sealed: &[u8], list_body: &[u8],
    device_ids: &[u8], now: u64) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ClientError>;

/// Phase 2 only. `history_body` is the 200 body of GET /v1/users/{id}/device-list?after=N:
/// [[version uint, blob bstr, ssk_signature b64, prev_hash b32]] ascending. For each row in order: blob
/// decodes (else E_CREDENTIAL); a row whose version equals the stored `device_list`'s and whose bytes equal
/// it is skipped; otherwise DeviceList::accept(Some(stored newest), own ssk_pub) must pass (E_DEVICE_LIST_STALE
/// for a version not greater or a broken prev_hash chain; E_CREDENTIAL for a bad signature), the row's
/// outer elements must equal the blob's (E_CORE_INPUT), and its user_id must be the stored user_id
/// (E_CREDENTIAL); the row becomes the stored newest. When a row was adopted and list_published is 0 and
/// the candidate's version is not greater than the new newest, the candidate is dropped
/// (device_list_body := the newest's PUT body, list_published := 1). An empty array changes nothing.
/// Returns [version uint, listed uint 0|1] of the stored newest, listed = this device present and unrevoked.
pub fn own_device_list_update(&mut self, history_body: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ClientError>;

/// Phase 2 only. [version uint, published uint 0|1, [[device_id b16, dsk_pub b32, tier uint, added_at uint,
/// revoked_at uint|null]]] of the stored newest (`device_list`); published = list_published.
pub fn own_device_list(&self) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ClientError>;

/// Phase 2 only: state_uploaded := 1.
pub fn state_sealed_uploaded(&mut self) -> Result<(), ClientError>;
```

`device_list_published()` (web-1) now also promotes the candidate: `device_list` := element 1 of the decoded `device_list_body`, `list_published` := 1. `device_list_body()` is unchanged (the candidate's PUT body). Refusal details the doubles mirror (task 10): a phase-3-only method (`enrol_session_sign`, `enrol_registered`, `enrol_complete`, `enrol_reset`) outside phase 3 → `E_CORE_STATE` "no enrolment is pending"; `enrol_begin` outside phase 0 → `E_CORE_STATE` "a signup is pending" (phase 1), "an identity exists" (phase 2), "an enrolment is pending" (phase 3); a phase-2-only method outside phase 2 → `E_CORE_NO_IDENTITY` with an empty detail; `enrol_session_sign`'s login bound → `E_CORE_INPUT` "login must be 1..=256 bytes"; `enrol_registered` with zeros → `E_CORE_INPUT` "user_id is all zero"; `own_device_list_update` → `E_CORE_INPUT` "history_body is malformed" / "history row elements disagree". **Attacker statements.** Step 2's `E_RECOVERY_KEY`: only the person typing a wrong key triggers it; the instance cannot (it cannot forge an AEAD under `K_header`). Step 3 refuses nothing: a stolen enrolled session (or the instance) can replace the state object with bytes that do not open, and the recovering device ignores them and rewrites the object, so the worst case is lost pins — none exist on browsers in web-2a (ruling 28). Step 4's `E_CREDENTIAL` on the served list: a hostile instance that serves a list it did not get from this user's SSK is refused and the enrolment stops (the honest instance serves the user's own list, which verifies). Step 5: an honest caller reaches it only by repeating a completed enrolment, and recovers by re-establishing. `own_device_list_update`'s `E_DEVICE_LIST_STALE`: an instance that serves a gap in the history, or a lower version, is refused; the honest instance serves a contiguous chain (L-HTTP-56). No refusal here can be triggered by another member or another user: these calls read only the own user's objects.

**L-CORE-27 error codes** (`src/client/error.rs`; amends web-1 L-CORE-02's table)

| code | raised for | detail |
|---|---|---|
| `E_RECOVERY_KEY` | the normalised recovery key is not 52 valid Crockford characters, or the root object does not open under it (AEAD failure) | empty, always (nothing about the key is ever written) |
| `E_DEVICE_LIST_STALE`, `E_CREDENTIAL`, `E_DEVICE_UNLISTED`, `E_TIER_MISMATCH` | as `ProtocolError::code()` (web-1 row 1), now reachable from L-CORE-26 | empty |
| `E_CORE_STATE` additions | "enrol record beside another phase", "no user recorded", "user already recorded", "device is listed", "credential does not verify" | as listed |

**L-CORE-28 recovery-key normalisation** (`src/identity/recovery.rs`, re-exported from `dilla_core::identity`; F2 allows paste)

```rust
/// Drops every ASCII space, tab, newline, carriage return, hyphen-minus, en dash (U+2013) and em dash (U+2014);
/// upper-cases ASCII a–z; maps 'I'→'1', 'L'→'1', 'O'→'0' (Crockford's folding); every other character is kept.
/// Pure; the result is what recovery_key_from_base32 is given (which still demands exactly 52 characters of
/// the Crockford alphabet, so 'U' and any non-ASCII character still fail there).
pub fn recovery_key_normalise(text: &str) -> String;
```

Vectors, asserted in Rust (`recovery.rs` tests) and in TypeScript (`packages/client-core/src/recovery-key.test.ts`, `normaliseRecoveryKey`, byte-identical rule): `"abcd-efgh"` → `"ABCDEFGH"`; `"AB CD\nEF"` → `"ABCDEF"`; `"il1o0"` → `"11100"`; `"A–B—C"` → `"ABC"`; `"ABCU"` → `"ABCU"` (U is kept and fails the parser). The recovery key the page shows at signup is `recovery_key_base32` output grouped in 13×4 (web-1); its normalisation is the identity.

### L-WASM — `dilla-core-wasm`

**L-WASM-20 facade exports** (`src/facade.rs`; the L-WASM-04 mapping; `BROWSER_ABI_VERSION = 5` in `src/lib.rs`, asserted by `tests/node.rs` and `src/lib.rs`'s own test)

New exports, one per L-CORE-21…26 method, same snake_case names: `group_row`, `mark_read`, `activity`, `settings`, `setting_put`, `setting_delete`, `enrol_begin`, `enrol_session_sign`, `enrol_registered`, `enrol_complete`, `enrol_reset`, `device_list_revoke`, `own_device_list_update`, `own_device_list`, `state_sealed_uploaded`. Changed exports: `group_create` and `group_join_external` take `community_id: Option<Vec<u8>>` (`None`/`undefined` → a DM; `Some` must be 16 bytes else `E_CORE_INPUT`); `sealed_objects` returns the 3-element shape. Argument mapping as L-WASM-04 except that the two secrets are **owned**: `enrol_complete` and `device_list_revoke` take `recovery_key: String` and `enrol_session_sign` takes `login: Vec<u8>` (the web-1 precedent `signup_request(password: Option<String>)`, `facade.rs:197-199`), each wrapped at once in `Zeroizing` and dropped — wiped — when the call returns; an `&str`/`&[u8]` parameter would leave wasm-bindgen's borrowed copy unwiped. The generated TypeScript is unchanged (`string`, `Uint8Array`). The facade pre-checks `login` (`E_CORE_INPUT` "login: expected 1..=256 bytes, got <n>", the `fixed_arg` form) before the call. `device_ids: &[u8]` → `&[u8]`; `now: u64` → `u64`. Every method throws `JsError` with the `ClientError` `Display`. The JS-side string is immutable and cannot be wiped, which is outside the core's reach (as for `kek_hex` in web-1).

### L-SQL — dillad store

**L-SQL-21 store methods** (both engines, sqlc; no migration — `backups`, `blobs`, `devices`, `device_lists` exist since `00010`/`00002`)

```go
// store.OpsBackups gains
InsertBackup(ctx context.Context, b BackupRow) error                   // INSERT without ON CONFLICT; a taken (user_id, kind, device_id, chunk_seq) is ErrConflict
GetBackup(ctx context.Context, userID id.ID, kind int32, deviceID id.ID, chunkSeq int64) (BackupRow, error)   // ErrNotFound
BackupRefersToBlob(ctx context.Context, blobID []byte) (bool, error)   // EXISTS over backups.blob_id
// store.Devices gains
ListDeviceListsAfter(ctx context.Context, userID id.ID, after uint64, limit int32) ([]DeviceListRow, error)   // version > after, ORDER BY version ASC, LIMIT limit
CountLiveDevicesByUser(ctx context.Context, userID id.ID) (int64, error)                                      // revoked_at IS NULL
ListDeviceCreationsSince(ctx context.Context, userID id.ID, since int64) ([]int64, error)                     // devices.created >= since, ORDER BY created ASC
```

`PutBackup` (the upsert) stays for kind 1. `ListCollectableBlobs` (both `blobs.sql` files) gains `AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM backups WHERE backups.blob_id = blobs.blob_id)`. The two literal method lists in `internal/store/contract_test.go` (`:41-44` `Devices`, `:226-228` `OpsBackups`) gain the six names; the third test derives its list. Bounds the store guards itself (both engines; `version` and `created` are signed 64-bit columns): `ListDeviceListsAfter` with `after > math.MaxInt64` or `limit <= 0` returns a non-nil empty slice without querying (SQLite reads `LIMIT -1` as no limit). `ListDeviceCreationsSince` counts **every** device row of the user with `created >= since`, revoked devices included (an enrolment revoked inside the hour still counts, so enrol-revoke-enrol cannot evade Q04's three per hour), and the account's first device included (ruling 32). The sweeper's per-row re-check (`internal/blob/gc.go:134-147`) is not changed: the residual window needs a byte-identical state object after `gc_grace`, which a fresh nonce per seal makes unreachable. **Mutation named:** remove the `backups` guard → the GC test that stores a root object, marks its blob unreferenced and sweeps goes red (the root bytes are collected).

### L-HTTP — routes

Common to every new row: CBOR bodies; `E` = enrolled session required, `P` = a pending session is admitted too (`Middleware(h, ScopePending)`), every pending-admitted route is **self-scoped for a pending session** (its path user, or implicitly the session's user); buckets are the delivery service's per-device ones (`dsMeter`, `read` for GET, `write` for PUT); `401 E_UNAUTHENTICATED` without a valid token; `403` for a pending scope on an E route (`E_FORBIDDEN`) and for a provisional scope on any of these (`E_PROVISIONAL_OUTSIDE_PAIRING`, what `auth.Sessions.Middleware` answers at `session.go:591-597`; code wins over the earlier draft of this rule); `429` and `500` can always be answered.

**L-HTTP-50 `PUT /v1/backups/{kind}/{chunk_seq}`** (new; C14, F3; `internal/api/backups.go`) — auth **E**, bucket write, idempotent (yes for kind 1, and for kind 0 a repeat of the same bytes answers 200). `kind` ∈ `0 | 1` as a decimal path segment, `chunk_seq` must be `0` (`404 E_NOT_FOUND` for any other kind or chunk, and for kind 2: this wire version serves no archive). Body `[object bstr]`, decoded with a body cap of **256 bytes** for kind 0 and **1,048,640 bytes** (1 MiB + 64) for kind 1 (`413 E_TOO_LARGE` over the cap). `object` must be a CBOR array `[1, nonce b12, ciphertext bstr]` (`400 E_INVALID_REQUEST` "object is not a stored header object"); for kind 0 its length must be exactly 103 (`400 E_INVALID_REQUEST`). `blob_id = SHA-256(object)`. `Deps.Blobs == nil` → `500 E_INTERNAL` "the backup store is not wired" on this route and on the single-object GET (the listing needs no store). Order of operations, as the attachment route's (`internal/api/blobs.go:190-246`; a filesystem write cannot sit inside a database transaction): `blob.Store.Put(ctx, blob_id, object, len)` first; then **one transaction**: `PutBlob` (insert-or-ignore, `unref_since NULL`), `ClearBlobUnreferenced(blob_id)` (bytes stored again inside the grace window leave it, `blobs.go:224-228`), then **kind 0:** `InsertBackup(user, 0, zero device, 0, blob_id)`; on `ErrConflict` the transaction returns a sentinel and **rolls back** (on Postgres a unique violation aborts the transaction it happens in), and the existing row is read **after** it with `GetBackup`: same `blob_id` → `200 [blob_id b32, size uint]`, different → `409 E_INVALID_REQUEST` "root object already stored" and nothing is written (F3 write-once; a refused upload's new file is recorded as an orphan as `blobs.go:293-311` does); **kind 1:** read the existing row (if any), `PutBackup` (upsert), and when the previous `blob_id` differs and `BackupRefersToBlob(previous)` is false → `MarkBlobUnreferenced(previous, now)`. Answer `201 [blob_id b32, size uint]` when the row was new, `200` when it was replaced or equal. Backup blobs count against `blobs.store_max_bytes` (`507 E_STORAGE_FULL` as the blob route) and not against the user quota. **Attacker statements:** the 409 of kind 0 is triggered only by the account's own enrolled session (the route is self-scoped by construction); a hijacked session cannot destroy the root object (it cannot replace it) and gains nothing from reading it (AEAD under `K_header`). Kind 1: a stolen enrolled session **can** replace the state object with bytes that do not open; the recovering device ignores an object it cannot open and rewrites it (L-CORE-26 step 3), so the worst case is lost pins, none of which exist on browsers in web-2a. The 1 MiB cap on kind 1 bounds what one account can store (one state object at a time; a replaced one is collected after `gc_grace`).

**L-HTTP-51 `GET /v1/backups`** (new) — auth **E or P**, bucket read. Answers `200 [[kind uint, chunk_seq uint, size uint, created uint]]` for the session's own user, ordered by `kind, chunk_seq` (`ListBackups` for kinds 0 and 1; kind 2 rows are not served), `[]` when none. No other status.

**L-HTTP-52 `GET /v1/backups/{kind}/{chunk_seq}`** (new) — auth **E or P**, bucket read. `kind` ∈ `0 | 1`, `chunk_seq = 0`, else `404 E_NOT_FOUND`; no row → `404 E_NOT_FOUND`; answers `200 [object bstr, created uint]` with the stored bytes read back through `blob.Store` (a stored blob that fails to read is `500`). Pending sessions reach this route so that an enrolling browser can fetch the root and state objects before it holds a credential (protocol/02 § Device sessions item 4 as amended).

**L-HTTP-53 `DELETE /v1/backups/{kind}/{chunk_seq}`** (new, mounted) — auth E; answers `501 E_INTERNAL` "DELETE /v1/backups is not served at wire 1" through `notImplemented` (the `PATCH /v1/accounts/me` precedent). Q27.

**L-HTTP-54 establish with registration, the device-list gate, the cap and the rate** (changed; C13, Q04, Q26; `internal/auth/session.go`, `internal/api/sessions.go`, `api.go`; protocol/02 § Device sessions items 2 and 4, protocol/09 § Devices)

Body `[nonce b32, purpose uint, sig b64, registration array|bstr|null, login bstr|null]`. Element 3 is read **only when `login` is present**; then it must be the five-element array `[device_id b16, dsk_pub b32, tier uint 0|1, signer_tier uint 0|1, credential bstr 1..=8192]` (the `POST /v1/devices` body, validated by the same `validate`) — a bstr or null there with `login` present is `400 E_INVALID_REQUEST` "registration array required"; with `login` absent, element 3 is ignored whatever its type (the testkit sends a bstr). `login` is the assertion's UTF-8 bytes as a bstr (protocol/09's `tstr` assertion sent as bytes; DEV-W2-18). `EstablishRequest` gains `Registration *DeviceRegistration` (nil when absent). `issue()`:

1. nonce and signature length, nonce taken (as today).
2. **Registration path** (`Login` present and no device row for the path id): `Registration` must be present and its `device_id` equal the path id (`400 E_INVALID_REQUEST` "device_id does not match"; a mismatch with `Registration` absent is the 400 above); **`Registration.tier` and `signer_tier` must both be `1`** (`400 E_INVALID_REQUEST` "assertion registration is for browser devices": the pairing ceremony of protocol/03 is the native path, and a `native` row would mint 30-day sessions and the `app` label for a browser); `sig` verified against `Registration.dsk_pub` over the preimage; the assertion spent (`Assertions.Spend`: unknown, expired, used, second factor outstanding → `401 E_UNAUTHENTICATED`; the assertion is spent **before** the list, cap and rate checks, since the asserted user is known only from `Spend`, so every refusal below costs the person a fresh login); the asserted user must not be disabled or deleted (`403 E_FORBIDDEN`; the password login already refuses a disabled account, `auth.go:209`, so this is a race); `DeviceLists.ListedKeys(asserted user)`: `ErrNoDeviceList` → `401 E_UNAUTHENTICATED` (Q26: assertion registration is refused for a user with no list); any other error → `401`; `CountLiveDevicesByUser ≥ cfg.MaxDevicesPerUser` → `403 E_FORBIDDEN` "device cap reached"; `creations = ListDeviceCreationsSince(user, now − 3599)` (a creation leaves the window exactly 3600 s after it; with `now − 3600` the boundary second would refuse with `retry_after_ms = 0`), `len(creations) ≥ cfg.EnrolmentsPerHour` → `429 E_RATE_LIMITED` with `retry_after_ms = (creations[len − limit] + 3600 − now) × 1000` (equal to the oldest's when `len == limit`; always ≥ 1000); then in one transaction `CreateDevice` (the row with `verified_at NULL`, `tier 1`, `credential_blob` = the placeholder) and `mint(…, ScopePending)`. Answer `201` as today with `scope = 1`.
3. **Ordinary path** (a row exists): revoked, key length, signature, user disabled — as today. With `Login` present: the assertion spent, same user, no second factor → `ScopePending` (as today). Without `Login`: `scope = ScopeEnrolled` **only if** `DeviceLists.ListedKeys(user)` returns `ErrNoDeviceList` (the no-list clause: web-1's resume and ensure, the Go fixtures, the testkit) or contains `device.DSKPub`; a listed user whose newest list does not name this key → `ScopePending`; any other error (verifier unavailable, list does not verify) → `401 E_UNAUTHENTICATED`. `purpose = 2` still mints `ScopeProvisional` (unchanged). `Sessions.DeviceLists` nil → every no-login establish is `401` (fail closed); `internal/dillad/server_test.go`'s dependency guard asserts it is wired.
4. `POST /v1/devices` is mounted `enrolled` (loses P: the registration path is the one way a pending device comes to exist).

```go
// internal/auth
type DeviceLister interface { ListedKeys(ctx context.Context, userID id.ID) ([][]byte, error) }   // the unrevoked dsk_pubs of the newest verified list
var ErrNoDeviceList = errors.New("auth: the user has published no device list")
type DeviceRegistration struct { DeviceID id.ID; DSKPub []byte; Tier, SignerTier uint8; Credential []byte }
// Sessions gains the field `DeviceLists DeviceLister`, set by the composition root.
// internal/config: Session gains MaxDevicesPerUser int `toml:"max_devices_per_user"` (default 8, valid 1..=64) and
// EnrolmentsPerHour int `toml:"enrolments_per_hour"` (default 3, valid 1..=60).
```

**Attacker statements.** The no-list 401 (step 2): a stolen host password alone cannot create a device row for an account whose owner never published a list (gap-G7 §2); an honest person enrolling into a web-1 account always has list v1. The pending scope for an unlisted device (step 3): a stolen password yields only a pending session until the recovery key signs list v+1; the honest enroller's next establish after its PUT is enrolled. The cap and the rate: the registration path creates a live (`revoked_at NULL`), unlisted row for every spent assertion, and the cap counts live rows, so **a password holder without the recovery key can register at most `EnrolmentsPerHour` rows per hour and reach the cap in ⌈cap ÷ rate⌉ hours (three hours at the defaults), after which the owner's own enrolment is refused with `signin.error.deviceCap`**; the owner clears it without the key: Settings → Devices lists those rows as `not yet in the device list` and their `remove` runs `DELETE /v1/devices/{id}` (L-HTTP-73; the row is in no signed list, so no list changes), and the rows are evidence of the compromise the owner then acts on with a password change. An honest person reaches 8 live devices by owning 8, and 3 enrolments per hour by enrolling 3; the account's first device counts in its first hour (ruling 32). The verifier-unavailable 401: a dillad started without its wasm runtime refuses every establish rather than admit unlisted devices — the operator sees it at once (`internal/dillad` refuses to start without a runtime, so this is a defence in depth).

**L-HTTP-55 `PUT /v1/users/{user_id}/device-list` verifies, and a revoking list revokes** (changed; Q27; DEV-W2-16, DEV-W2-24; protocol/02 item 6, protocol/09 § Devices) — auth **E or P**, self only (`403 E_FORBIDDEN` for another user, both scopes), bucket write. Body as today `[version uint, blob bstr, ssk_signature b64, prev_hash b32]` (cap 64 KiB). Checks in order: the blob decodes in Go as a 6-element CBOR array whose element 2 (`version`) equals the body's `version` and element 3 (`prev_hash`) equals the body's `prev_hash`, and whose element 5 equals `ssk_signature` (`400 E_INVALID_REQUEST` "device list elements disagree"); `Deps.DeviceLists.Verify(ctx, blob, users.ssk_pub, user_id) ([]mlswasi.DeviceListEntry, error)` (the guest's `device_list_entries`: signature and `user_id`; the decoded entries carry the `DeviceID` and `Revoked` the revocation action needs) must pass: an `*mlswasi.ABIError` with code `E_CREDENTIAL` → `400 E_INVALID_REQUEST` "device list does not verify"; any other verifier error (no runtime, a guest fault) → `500 E_INTERNAL` (a fault of the instance is not reported as the client's bad list); `newest = GetDeviceList(user)`: with none, `version` must be 1 and `prev_hash` 32 zero bytes; with one, `version` must equal `newest.Version + 1` and `prev_hash` must equal `SHA-256(newest.Blob)` (`409 E_INVALID_REQUEST` "device-list version <n> is not the next version" — the client refetches and rebuilds). Then in one transaction: `PutDeviceList`; for every entry of the verified list with `Revoked` whose device row exists, is this user's and has `revoked_at IS NULL`: `RevokeDevice(at = now)` and `DeleteSessionsByDevice` (the sessions of the publishing device included, when it revoked itself); after the commit `OnRevoke(device)` for each (sockets closed, call cut) and `204`; then `Deps.AfterDeviceList func(ctx context.Context, userID id.ID, revoked []id.ID)` (the field's type changes; every caller — `devices.go:160-162`, `server.go:311`, `devicelist_hook_test.go` — is in task 8's files) runs `SyncUserDMs` (as today) and `api.RemoveRevokedDevices(ctx context.Context, repo store.Repository, dsvc DS, devices []id.ID) error`: for every revoked device and every group of `GroupsForDevice(device)`, `ProposeRemoveDevice(group, device, id.New())` (errors logged, the loop continues; the DS comes from the composition root's closure, which already holds it, `server.go:311-316` — no `Deps.Delivery`). `Deps.DeviceLists DeviceListVerifier` nil → `500 E_INTERNAL` "device-list verifier is not wired" (fail closed). The proof of the Remove is split (the composition root has no MLS client): an `internal/api` unit test with the existing `recordingDS` proves one `ProposeRemoveDevice` per (group, revoked device) from `GroupsForDevice`, error isolation and the nil-DS refusal; `web2a_routes_test.go` seeds one group with the revoked device's leaf and asserts through a captured `slog` handler on `dillad.Options.Log` that the hook attempted that Remove; the real Remove of a real leaf is proven by task 9's HARNESS `revoke` verb and task 21's e2e. **Attacker statements.** Only the user's own sessions reach the route; the verification makes a stolen *session* unable to publish an unverifiable list (DEV-W2-24's self-lockout) because it holds no SSK; a stolen SSK is the account (protocol/03). The 409 is triggered by a race between two of the user's own devices and is cured by a refetch. The revocation action acts only on devices the user's SSK signed as revoked.

**L-HTTP-56 `GET /v1/users/{user_id}/device-list[?after=N]`** (changed; Q27; DEV-W2-32) — auth **E or P**: enrolled sessions may read any user's list (unchanged, DEV-W2-34 stays open for web-2c), a pending session only its own (`403 E_FORBIDDEN`); bucket read. Without `after`: the newest row as today, `200 [version, blob, ssk_signature, prev_hash]`, `404 E_NOT_FOUND` when none. With `after=N` (a decimal uint that fits `int64`; malformed or above `math.MaxInt64` → `400 E_INVALID_REQUEST`): `200 [[version, blob, ssk_signature, prev_hash]]` of the stored rows with `version > N`, ascending, at most **64** rows (`ListDeviceListsAfter(user, N, 64)`), `[]` when none (never 404). Because every stored version after this plan is verified and contiguous (L-HTTP-55), the history is a chain a client can walk. **Attacker statement:** reading a history refuses nothing; it exposes only what the user published, which the newest list already revealed.

**L-HTTP-57 the pending surface** (protocol/02 item 4 as amended by task 7): a pending session reaches exactly `GET /v1/backups`, `GET /v1/backups/{kind}/{chunk_seq}`, `GET /v1/users/{own}/device-list` (with or without `after`), `PUT /v1/users/{own}/device-list`, and the session routes that need no session. Everything else answers `403 E_FORBIDDEN`. `web2a_routes_test.go` (task 8) proves each of the four with a pending token and proves `POST /v1/devices` and `POST /v1/keypackages` refuse it.

**L-TS-21 the enrolment flow, the backup upload step and the own list** (`src/account/enrol.ts`; amends `session.ts`, `signup.ts`)

```ts
export class Enrol {
  constructor(deps: { core: CorePort; routes: Routes; session: Session; now(): number });
  /** POST /v1/auth/password/login. Keeps the assertion in a private field, never in a slice or a store. */
  login(username: string, password: string): Promise<{ needsTotp: boolean }>;
  /** POST /v1/auth/totp/verify with the held assertion. The assertion is TAKEN OUT of the field before the
   *  request (the server spends it before checking the code, internal/api/auth.go:609-633); on success the
   *  new assertion is held; on any failure the field stays empty, so the next totp() or register() throws
   *  Error('E_NO_ASSERTION') and the person logs in again. */
  totp(code: string): Promise<void>;
  /** Requires a held assertion with no factor outstanding (else Error('E_NO_ASSERTION'), no request); takes it
   *  out of the field first (dropped whatever happens). Device: phase 0 → enrolBegin(instanceId).deviceId;
   *  phase 3 with userId === null → identity().deviceId (a lost answer to the pending establish must not spend
   *  the cap and the rate twice; the server finds the row and answers pending, L-HTTP-54 step 3); any other
   *  phase → CoreError('E_CORE_STATE', 'register needs phase 0 or an unregistered enrolment'). Then
   *  postChallenge → enrolSessionSign(nonce, utf8(assertion)) (the UTF-8 bytes zero-filled in a finally) →
   *  postSessionPending; the answer's scope must be 1 (else Error('E_SESSION_SCOPE'), nothing stored);
   *  sessionStore; enrolRegistered(userId). Every refusal propagates unchanged (401, 403, 429, 400) and the
   *  enrol record stays (phase 3, no user) for the next register. */
  register(instanceId: Id): Promise<{ userId: Id }>;
  /** getBackup(0), getBackup(1), getDeviceList(userId) (pending-scoped). A missing root (404) is
   *  Error('E_NO_BACKUP') with no further request; a missing state (404) is NOT an error: state = new
   *  Uint8Array(0) (L-CORE-26 step 3 treats it as no pins); a missing list cannot happen after L-HTTP-54 and
   *  is Error('E_NO_BACKUP'). listBody = the record's raw bytes (row 72). */
  fetch(userId: Id): Promise<{ root: Uint8Array; state: Uint8Array; listBody: Uint8Array }>;
  /** enrolComplete (the key passed unchanged: Rust normalises; a CoreError propagates and nothing is sent) →
   *  publishDeviceList(core, routes) (its 409 rule below; an Error('E_DEVICE_UNLISTED') from it is rethrown as
   *  Error('E_LIST_RACE'): the core is then in phase 2 with an unlisted identity, which only a wipe cures,
   *  L-TS-23) → session.establish() (purpose 0, scope 0, false → Error('E_SESSION_SCOPE')) →
   *  putBackup(1, stateSealed) → stateSealedUploaded. */
  complete(recoveryKey: string, fetched: { root; state; listBody }, username: string): Promise<void>;
  /** enrolReset(); the pending session is left to expire (no E route can delete it). */
  reset(): void;
}
/** On every ready and after an enrolment: listBackups(); with no kind-0 row and a sealedObjects().root → putBackup(0, root)
 *  (a 409 is swallowed: the root is there); with no kind-1 row or sealedObjects().stateUploaded === false and a state →
 *  putBackup(1, state) then stateSealedUploaded(). Errors propagate; the controller logs none and retries on the next ready. */
export function ensureBackups(core: CorePort, routes: Routes): Promise<void>;
/** = adoptServedList(core, routes, userId, await routes.getDeviceList(userId)). */
export function refreshOwnDeviceList(core: CorePort, routes: Routes, userId: Id): Promise<{ version: bigint; listed: boolean }>;
// packages/client-core/src/account/signup.ts
export const DEVICE_LIST_HISTORY_PAGE = 64;   // L-HTTP-56's row cap
/** own = ownDeviceList(); served null or served.version <= own.version → { version: own.version, listed } from the
 *  stored entries, no request. Else loop from after = own.version: page = getDeviceListHistory(userId, after);
 *  count 0 → the last result; result = ownDeviceListUpdate(page.raw); return when count < DEVICE_LIST_HISTORY_PAGE,
 *  or result.version >= served.version, or result.version <= after (no progress); else after = result.version.
 *  Core errors (E_DEVICE_LIST_STALE, E_CREDENTIAL) propagate. */
export function adoptServedList(core: CorePort, routes: Routes, userId: Id, served: DeviceListRecord | null): Promise<{ version: bigint; listed: boolean }>;
export function publishDeviceList(core: CorePort, routes: Routes): Promise<void>;   // signature unchanged
```

`Session.establishOnce` (web-1 L-TS-06): the expected scope is `1` when `identity().phase === 3` and `0` otherwise; a mismatch throws `Error('E_SESSION_SCOPE')` as today; a confirmed 401 in phase 3 clears nothing. **`publishDeviceList`'s 409 rule (one rule for both callers; it also handles a lost answer to the device's own PUT, which the idempotent `HttpClient` retries against its own stored version):** returns at once when `identity().listPublished`; `putDeviceList(userId, deviceListBody())`; success → `deviceListPublished()`. Rules (each a test in task 12): (1) `row(g)` is `core.groupRow(g)`; the ready sweep iterates `core.groups()` once. (2) `resyncGroup` builds its `ExpectedGroup` with the row's `communityId` (null for a DM) and never throws `E_NO_COMMUNITY` (the code is deleted from `SyncError`). (3) `openChannel` with `textGroupId === null` and `communityId === null` (a DM whose group is unknown) first calls `getChannel(channelId)` to learn `textGroupId`; still null → the DM has no group yet: the client **registers** it (`groupCreate(g, null, channelId, …)` → `postGroup`), as protocol/09:394-396 lets a participant do. (4) **Join-all:** after the ready sweep of every state-2 group, the engine walks `expected()` in order (channels first, then DMs), and for every group with no local row in state 2 or 3 runs the join of rule 6 (web-1) on that group's lane with the welcome step first and the external join next, **one group at a time** (`joinAllConcurrency`), never registering a group (a channel with `textGroupId === null` is skipped: nobody has written there, so nothing is unread), reporting `onJoinAll` after each; a refused join is counted `failed` and retried on the next ready or after `joinAllRetryMs`, whichever comes first; a join-all join in flight does not delay an `openChannel` of another group (different lanes) and an `openChannel` of the same group awaits the lane and returns the result — the open's join job (`channel.ts:143`) re-reads the row first and returns without joining when it is already in state 2 (no second external commit). (5) A live frame for a group join-all has not reached is held as today (≤ 512). (6) `stop()` ends the pass. (7) `setExpected` with a set that gained a group runs the welcome step before that group's external join, so a held Welcome for a DM another participant opened joins Welcome-first once the controller has learned the DM (`onUnexpectedWelcome` → `loadDms()` → `setExpected`). (8) Card 29 (web-1): a Welcome judged outcome 2 is deleted at the instance; a Welcome judged outcome 3 is kept. `SyncDeps.onJoinAll` and `onUnexpectedWelcome` are required members: `controller.ts:359-363` gets no-ops in task 12 (task 14 replaces them) and `sync/testing/harness.ts:34-53` a recorder. **Mutation named:** make join-all register groups for `textGroupId === null` channels → the "join-all registers nothing" model test goes red (a `postGroup` call appears).

```ts
export type Command = /* the web-1 thirteen */
  | { m: 'signInBegin' }                                         // needs-signup → signin-login

  | { m: 'signInTotp'; code: string }                            // signin-totp → signin-key
  | { m: 'signInKey'; recoveryKey: string }                      // signin-key → ready
  | { m: 'signInCancel' }                                        // signin-* → needs-signup
  | { m: 'refreshDevices' }                                      // ready: GET /v1/devices + own list → slice devices
  | { m: 'revokeDevice'; deviceId: string; recoveryKey: string | null } // ready: another device; the key is required for a listed device, ignored (null) for an unlisted live row
  | { m: 'signOutRevoke'; recoveryKey: string }                  // ready: this device → store wiped → cleared
  | { m: 'forgetBrowser' }                                       // ready: sessions deleted, store wiped → cleared
  | { m: 'markRead'; channelId: string }                         // ready
  | { m: 'setSetting'; key: string; value: string | null }       // ready; null deletes; key must match L-TS-25, value its allowed set
  | { m: 'openDm'; userId: string };                             // ready → { channelId }
```
