  `index.ts` exports the seven components and their seven prop types. The DOM contract the screens (tasks 18, 19) and the e2e (task 21) rely on: `Toggle` is a `<button type="button" role="switch" aria-checked>` whose accessible name is `label` and whose `id` is `id` (named by `aria-label={label}`, or with `showLabel` by `aria-labelledby="<id>-label"`, the visible `<span id="<id>-label" class="d-toggle__label">` before it); `Segmented` is a `role="radiogroup"` element with `id={id}`, named through `aria-labelledby` by `label`, of `<button type="button" role="radio" aria-checked>` options named by their labels; `SettingsRow` is a `role="group"` named by its visible label (`id="<id>-label"`) and described by its hint (`id="<id>-hint"`); `SettingsNav` is `<nav aria-label={label}>` of buttons named by their labels, the active one `aria-current="page"`; `SettingsFrame`'s root is a `<dialog class="d-settings-frame" aria-modal="true">` labelled by its `<h1 tabIndex=-1>`, whose close control is a button named `closeLabel`; `DeviceRow` is an `<li class="d-device-row" data-tier="web|native" data-own="true"?>` with `name`, `tierLabel`, `ownLabel`, `state` and `lastSeen` each in its own `<span>`, and its action a `Button` named by its label, described by the name, `data-variant="danger"` when `danger`; `RecoveryKeyField` is an `<input type="text">` with `id={id}` named by `label`, its hint `id="<id>-hint"`, its error `id="<id>-error"` inside `role="alert"`.

**Requirements:**
1. `Toggle` (L-UI-20; brief "Accessibility model"; Mesh `settings.css:206-226`): a native `<button type="button" role="switch">`, `aria-checked` the state. Without `showLabel` (or with `showLabel` false) the switch is named by `aria-label={label}` and draws no text (the visible label is the `SettingsRow`'s, WCAG 2.5.3: the same text). With `showLabel` the component renders `<span id="<id>-label" class="d-toggle__label">{label}</span>` before the switch and names the switch by `aria-labelledby="<id>-label"`, with no `aria-label` (the mute switch beside a `Segmented` in a per-channel row whose visible label is the channel's name: the word `mute` is seen and heard). In both forms `aria-describedby="<id>-hint"` when `hint` is given (the hint is a visible `<span>` after the switch). Click, `Space` and `Enter` call `onChange(!checked)` once. `disabled` sets `aria-disabled="true"` and never the native `disabled`, keeps the switch focusable, and makes activation do nothing (Global Constraints "Accessibility rules"). The state is shown by the knob's position as well as by colour (WCAG 1.4.1). The pointer target is at least 2.75rem × 1.5rem (44 × 24 CSS px, WCAG 2.5.8).
2. `Segmented` (L-UI-21; Mesh `settings.css:228-246`): the label is a `d-sr-only` `<span id="<id>-label">` (the visible label is the row's), the group `role="radiogroup"` with `id={id}` and `aria-labelledby`; one `<button type="button" role="radio">` per option in order, `aria-checked` on the one whose `value` equals `value`; one tab stop: the checked option has `tabIndex=0` and the others `-1` (the first option when none is checked). `ArrowRight`/`ArrowDown` move to the next option and `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowUp` to the previous one, wrapping; `Home`/`End` to the ends; each move focuses the option and calls `onChange(value)` unless it is already the value (the ARIA radio-group pattern); a click calls `onChange`; a key with Alt, Ctrl, Meta or Shift is left alone. The checked option is marked by an underline bar (`box-shadow`) and weight as well as colour. Each option is at least 1.5rem × 1.5rem.
3. `SettingsRow` (L-UI-22; Mesh `settings.css:161-171`): `<div role="group" class="d-settings-row" aria-labelledby="<id>-label" aria-describedby="<id>-hint"?>` with the visible label and hint on the left and the control on the right; it wraps under the label when the row is narrower than the two (flex-wrap, no breakpoint).
4. `SettingsNav` (L-UI-23): `<nav aria-label>` → `<ul role="list">` → `<li><button type="button" aria-current="page"?>`; roving focus through `useRovingFocus` (one tab stop; `ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown`/`Home`/`End`, no wrap, never selects); `Enter`, `Space` and a click call `onSelect(id)`. The current item is marked by a left bar (`box-shadow`) and weight as well as colour. Each item is at least 2rem tall.
5. `SettingsFrame` (L-UI-24; brief "Layout": 960 × 640 with a 220px nav; Mesh `settings.css:12-110`): a native `<dialog>` that stays mounted, opened with `showModal()` and closed with `close()` from an effect on `open` (so the browser returns focus to whatever opened it), closed on unmount too; when it opens, its `<h1 tabIndex=-1>` (the title) takes focus, also on every reopen; `aria-labelledby` points at the `<h1>`; `Escape` (a `keydown` on the dialog, `preventDefault`) and the native `cancel` event (`preventDefault`) call `onClose`; a click on the backdrop (the dialog element itself) calls `onClose`; the content exists only while `open` (a closed frame leaks no text). Layout: the navigation column (13.75rem) holds the `<h1>` then `nav`; the content column holds a bar with the close `Button` (`variant="ghost"`, `keyHint="esc"`, named `closeLabel`) then `children` in a scrolling body. Tab order: `<h1>` (focused by script, not a tab stop) → the navigation's one stop → the close button → the content (Global Constraints "Keyboard map"). Under 45rem (720px) of viewport the frame fills the viewport (100vw × 100dvh, no border); under 45rem of the frame's own width the navigation stacks above the content; both rules live in `base.css` (web-1's rule: no breakpoint outside it). The script-focused title draws no ring (design ruling 23(h)); every operable control keeps it.
6. `DeviceRow` (L-UI-25; F9: the browser's tier is shown here and nowhere in the chrome): one `<li>`; first line: the name, the tier tag, and the own tag when `own` and `ownLabel`; second line, when either is given: `state`, a decorative `·` (`aria-hidden`) when both are given, `lastSeen`; on the right the action, when given, as a `Button` (`variant="danger"` when `danger`, else `default`; size `md`) with `aria-describedby` the name's `<span>` (so "remove" is heard with the device it removes). `data-tier` is `tier`; `data-own="true"` when `own`. No English is hard-coded.
7. `RecoveryKeyField` (L-UI-26; F2 and WCAG 3.3.8: paste allowed; `protocol/03-identity.md` "Recovery"): a `<label for>` and an `<input type="text" autoComplete="off" autoCapitalize="characters" spellCheck={false} inputMode="text">` with no `maxLength` and no `name` (a pasted grouped key of 64 characters must fit; nothing offers to remember it); the value is shown exactly as typed (no `text-transform`), in the mono face with letter spacing; `onChange` receives the raw text on every change; nothing cancels paste, copy or cut; the hint and the error are the description in that order, the error marks the field `aria-invalid` and sits in `role="alert"`; `disabled` disables the input (a running submit; the pressed button keeps focus). The hint is not a live region (flow 03 "Focus and announcements").
8. Every new component uses design tokens only (no hex, no px font size; rem boxes), renders in the three themes and under reduced motion (no transition), and passes `vitest-axe` with no serious or critical violation and the Storybook test-runner's axe gate, focus-ring check and dialog-ring check (Global Constraints "Accessibility rules"). The test-runner enables axe's `target-size` for story titles under `Settings/` (L-UI title list; `Form/` is already strict).
9. Stories, one per state, titled `Form/Toggle` (Off, On, Disabled, WithLabel), `Form/Segmented` (NotifyDefault, Theme, ChannelMode), `Form/RecoveryKeyField` (Empty, Typing, Pasted, WrongKey, Disabled), `Settings/SettingsRow` (Permission, NotifyDefault, PerChannel), `Settings/SettingsNav` (Devices, Notifications), `Settings/DeviceRow` (ThisBrowser, OtherBrowser, App, Unlisted, Removed), `Settings/SettingsFrame` (Devices, Notifications, Narrow): 25 stories, 75 screenshots under `target/ui-screens/web-2a/` (F16). The `Unlisted` row carries its `remove` action (ruling 30); the frame's Devices section draws the count line `3 devices` (ruling 33) over three live rows and one removed row; the per-channel rows use the mute `Toggle` with `showLabel` and the `notify.channels.body` text of L-COPY-02.
10. No string literal or JSX text in the new files uses a word `scripts/check-ui-copy.mjs:5-11` forbids (tests and stories are scanned).
11. Lesson (e): this task adds no refusal. Lessons (c), (d), (f), (g): no browser e2e, no server behaviour, no store.

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';

import { Toggle, type ToggleProps } from './Toggle.tsx';

// L-COPY-02: notify.mute names a channel's mute switch; notify.permission.label and notify.body are
// the label and hint texts of a Settings → Notifications row.
const HINT = 'Desktop notifications show while a dilla tab is open. Nothing is shown when every tab is closed.';

function Controlled(p: Omit<ToggleProps, 'checked' | 'onChange'> & { initial?: boolean; onValue?: (v: boolean) => void }) {
  const { initial = false, onValue, ...rest } = p;
  const [checked, setChecked] = useState(initial);
  return <Toggle {...rest} checked={checked} onChange={v => { setChecked(v); onValue?.(v); }} />;
}

describe('Toggle', () => {
  it('is a button with the switch role, named by its label, its state in aria-checked', () => {
    const { container } = render(<Toggle id="mute-general" label="mute" checked={false} onChange={() => {}} />);
    const sw = screen.getByRole('switch', { name: 'mute' });
    expect(sw.tagName).toBe('BUTTON');
    expect(sw).toHaveAttribute('type', 'button');
    expect(sw).toHaveAttribute('id', 'mute-general');
    expect(sw).toHaveAttribute('aria-checked', 'false');
    expect(sw).toHaveAttribute('aria-label', 'mute');
    expect(sw).not.toHaveAttribute('aria-labelledby');
    expect(container.firstElementChild).toHaveClass('d-toggle');
    expect(container.querySelector('.d-toggle__label')).toBeNull();
  });

  it('with showLabel draws the label before the switch and is named by that visible text', () => {
    const { container } = render(<Toggle id="mute-general" label="mute" checked={false} onChange={() => {}} showLabel hint={HINT} />);
    const sw = screen.getByRole('switch', { name: 'mute' });
    const text = container.querySelector('.d-toggle__label');
    expect(text).not.toBeNull();
    expect(text).toHaveTextContent('mute');
    expect(text).toHaveAttribute('id', 'mute-general-label');
    expect(text?.tagName).toBe('SPAN');
    expect(sw).toHaveAttribute('aria-labelledby', 'mute-general-label');
    expect(sw).not.toHaveAttribute('aria-label');
    expect(text!.compareDocumentPosition(sw) & Node.DOCUMENT_POSITION_FOLLOWING).toBeTruthy();
    expect(sw).toHaveAccessibleDescription(HINT);
  });

  it('toggles on click, Space and Enter and reports each new state', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();

    await user.click(sw);

    expect(sw).toHaveAttribute('aria-checked', 'true');
```

```tsx
] as const;

function Controlled({ initial = 'system', onValue }: { initial?: string; onValue?: (v: string) => void }) {
  const [value, setValue] = useState(initial);
  return (
    <>
      <button type="button">before</button>
      <Segmented id="theme" label="Theme" options={THEMES} value={value} onChange={v => { setValue(v); onValue?.(v); }} />
      <button type="button">after</button>
    </>
  );
}
const radio = (name: string) => screen.getByRole('radio', { name });

describe('Segmented', () => {
  it('is a radiogroup named by its label, one radio button per option, the value checked', () => {
    const { container } = render(<Segmented id="theme" label="Theme" options={THEMES} value="mesh" onChange={() => {}} />);
    const group = screen.getByRole('radiogroup', { name: 'Theme' });
    expect(group).toHaveAttribute('id', 'theme');

    expect(radios.map(r => r.textContent)).toEqual(['system', 'mesh', 'light', 'high contrast']);
    expect(radios.map(r => r.tagName)).toEqual(['BUTTON', 'BUTTON', 'BUTTON', 'BUTTON']);
    expect(radios.map(r => r.getAttribute('aria-checked'))).toEqual(['false', 'true', 'false', 'false']);
  });

  it('is one tab stop, on the checked option', async () => {

    await user.tab();
    expect(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'after' })).toHaveFocus();
    await user.tab({ shift: true });
    expect(radio('light')).toHaveFocus();
  });

  it('moves the selection with the arrows, wrapping, and with Home and End', async () => {

    expect(radio('high contrast')).toHaveFocus();
    await user.keyboard('{ArrowDown}');

  });

  it('selects on click and leaves a modified arrow alone', async () => {

    expect(radio('light')).toHaveFocus();
    await user.keyboard('{Alt>}{ArrowRight}{/Alt}');

  it('has no serious axe violations', async () => {
```

```tsx
    expect(items.map(b => b.getAttribute('aria-current'))).toEqual([null, 'page', null]);

    await user.keyboard('{ArrowUp}');

    await user.keyboard('{End}');
```

```tsx
import { render, screen, within } from '@testing-library/react';
import userEvent from '@testing-library/user-event';
import { describe, it, expect, vi } from 'vitest';
import { SettingsFrame, type SettingsFrameProps } from './SettingsFrame.tsx';
import { SettingsNav } from '../SettingsNav/SettingsNav.tsx';
import { expectNoAxeViolations } from '../test/setup.ts';

// L-COPY-02: settings.title, settings.close, settings.nav.*, devices.title, devices.refresh.
const ITEMS = [{ id: 'devices', label: 'devices' }, { id: 'notifications', label: 'notifications' }, { id: 'appearance', label: 'appearance' }] as const;
function props(over: Partial<SettingsFrameProps> = {}): SettingsFrameProps {
  return {
    open: true, title: 'Settings', closeLabel: 'Close settings', onClose: vi.fn(),
    nav: <SettingsNav label="settings sections" items={ITEMS} activeId="devices" onSelect={() => {}} />,
    children: <section aria-labelledby="devices-title"><h2 id="devices-title">Devices</h2><button type="button">refresh</button></section>,
    ...over,
  };
}

describe('SettingsFrame', () => {
  it('opens as a modal dialog named by its h1, and the h1 takes focus', () => {
    render(<SettingsFrame {...props()} />);
    const dialog = screen.getByRole('dialog', { name: 'Settings' });
    expect(dialog.tagName).toBe('DIALOG');
    expect(dialog).toHaveClass('d-settings-frame');
    expect(dialog).toHaveAttribute('aria-modal', 'true');
    expect(within(dialog).getByRole('heading', { level: 1, name: 'Settings' })).toHaveFocus();
  });

  it('holds the navigation and the section', () => {
    render(<SettingsFrame {...props()} />);
    const dialog = screen.getByRole('dialog', { name: 'Settings' });
    expect(within(dialog).getByRole('navigation', { name: 'settings sections' })).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(within(dialog).getByRole('heading', { level: 2, name: 'Devices' })).toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it('tabs from the heading to the navigation, the close button, then the section', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    render(<SettingsFrame {...props()} />);
    await user.tab();
    expect(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'devices' })).toHaveFocus();
    await user.tab();
    expect(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Close settings' })).toHaveFocus();
    await user.tab();
    expect(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'refresh' })).toHaveFocus();
  });

  it('calls onClose on Escape and from the close button', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const p = props();
    render(<SettingsFrame {...p} />);
    await user.keyboard('{Escape}');
    expect(p.onClose).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Close settings' }));
    expect(p.onClose).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
  });

  it('closes the native dialog when open flips to false, so the browser returns focus', () => {
    const close = vi.spyOn(HTMLDialogElement.prototype, 'close');
    const p = props();
    const { rerender } = render(<SettingsFrame {...p} />);
    expect(close).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    rerender(<SettingsFrame {...p} open={false} />);
    expect(close).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    close.mockRestore();
  });

  it('renders no content while closed', () => {
    render(<SettingsFrame {...props({ open: false })} />);
    expect(screen.queryByRole('dialog')).toBeNull();
    expect(screen.queryByRole('heading')).toBeNull();
    expect(screen.queryByRole('navigation')).toBeNull();
  });

  it('focuses the heading again when it reopens', () => {
    const p = props();
    const { rerender } = render(<SettingsFrame {...p} />);
    rerender(<SettingsFrame {...p} open={false} />);
    rerender(<SettingsFrame {...p} open />);
    expect(screen.getByRole('heading', { level: 1, name: 'Settings' })).toHaveFocus();
  });

  it('has no serious axe violations', async () => {
    const { container } = render(<div className="d-root"><SettingsFrame {...props()} /></div>);
    await expectNoAxeViolations(container);
  });
});
```

```tsx
import { expectNoAxeViolations } from '../test/setup.ts';

// L-COPY-02: signin.key.label, signin.key.hint, signin.error.wrongKey. The key is flow 02's sample key,
// never a real one, pasted as a person might: lower case, hyphenated, 64 characters.
const GROUPED = '7k3m-qw9d-x2rt-0pna-hv5c-j8ze-m4tb-s6yf-1gkd-r3wp-zn7h-c9qx-5tva';
const WRONG = 'This is not the recovery key of this account. Check every character.';

function Controlled(p: Omit<RecoveryKeyFieldProps, 'value' | 'onChange'> & { onValue?: (v: string) => void }) {
  const { onValue, ...rest } = p;
  const [value, setValue] = useState('');
  return <RecoveryKeyField {...rest} value={value} onChange={v => { setValue(v); onValue?.(v); }} />;
}

describe('RecoveryKeyField', () => {
  it('is a text input named by its label, with no autocomplete, no spellcheck, no name and no length limit', () => {
    const { container } = render(<RecoveryKeyField id="recovery-key" label="Recovery key" value="" onChange={() => {}} />);
    const input = screen.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Recovery key' });
    expect(container.firstElementChild).toHaveClass('d-recovery-key-field');
    expect(input).toHaveClass('d-recovery-key-field__input');
    expect(input).toHaveAttribute('id', 'recovery-key');
    expect(input).toHaveAttribute('type', 'text');
    expect(input).toHaveAttribute('autocomplete', 'off');
    expect(input).toHaveAttribute('autocapitalize', 'characters');
    expect(input).toHaveAttribute('spellcheck', 'false');
    expect(input).toHaveAttribute('inputmode', 'text');
    expect(input).not.toHaveAttribute('maxlength');
    expect(input).not.toHaveAttribute('name');
  });

  it('reports the raw text on every change and shows it as typed', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const onValue = vi.fn();
    render(<Controlled id="recovery-key" label="Recovery key" onValue={onValue} />);
    await user.type(screen.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Recovery key' }), 'ab-c');
    expect(onValue.mock.calls.map(c => c[0])).toEqual(['a', 'ab', 'ab-', 'ab-c']);
    expect(screen.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Recovery key' })).toHaveValue('ab-c');
  });

  it('takes a pasted grouped key whole: paste is never cancelled and nothing is cut off', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const onValue = vi.fn();
    render(<Controlled id="recovery-key" label="Recovery key" onValue={onValue} />);
    const input = screen.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Recovery key' });
    expect(fireEvent.paste(input)).toBe(true);
    await user.click(input);
    await user.paste(GROUPED);
    expect(input).toHaveValue(GROUPED);
    expect(onValue).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith(GROUPED);
  });

  it('binds the hint and the error as the description, marks the field invalid and announces the error', () => {
    render(<RecoveryKeyField id="recovery-key" label="Recovery key" value={GROUPED} onChange={() => {}} hint="52 of 52 characters" error={WRONG} />);
    const input = screen.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Recovery key' });
    expect(input).toHaveAccessibleDescription(`52 of 52 characters ${WRONG}`);
    expect(input).toHaveAttribute('aria-invalid', 'true');
    expect(screen.getByRole('alert')).toHaveTextContent(WRONG);
  });

  it('is described by the hint alone without an error, and by nothing without either', () => {
    const { rerender } = render(<RecoveryKeyField id="recovery-key" label="Recovery key" value="7K3M" onChange={() => {}} hint="4 of 52 characters" />);
    const input = screen.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Recovery key' });
    expect(input).toHaveAccessibleDescription('4 of 52 characters');
    expect(input).not.toHaveAttribute('aria-invalid');
    rerender(<RecoveryKeyField id="recovery-key" label="Recovery key" value="7K3M" onChange={() => {}} />);
    expect(input).not.toHaveAttribute('aria-describedby');
    expect(screen.queryByRole('alert')).toBeNull();
  });

  it('disables the input', () => {
    render(<RecoveryKeyField id="recovery-key" label="Recovery key" value={GROUPED} onChange={() => {}} disabled />);
    expect(screen.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Recovery key' })).toBeDisabled();
  });

  it('has no serious axe violations with a hint and an error', async () => {
    const { container } = render(
      <div className="d-root"><RecoveryKeyField id="recovery-key" label="Recovery key" value={GROUPED} onChange={() => {}} hint="52 of 52 characters" error={WRONG} /></div>,
    );
    await expectNoAxeViolations(container);
  });
});
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement the arrow rule, `Toggle`, `Segmented` and `SettingsRow`**

`packages/ui/src/internal/arrow-select.ts` (open the file with a doc comment saying it is the wrapping arrow rule of single-select groups, the radio group and the tab list). `arrowIndex(event, from, count, axis)`: returns `null` when any of `altKey`, `ctrlKey`, `metaKey`, `shiftKey` is set, or when `count <= 0`; `ArrowRight` → `(from + 1) % count`; `ArrowLeft` → `(from - 1 + count) % count`; with `axis === 'both'` also `ArrowDown` as `ArrowRight` and `ArrowUp` as `ArrowLeft`; `Home` → `0`; `End` → `count - 1`; any other key → `null`. Pure; no DOM.

`Toggle.tsx` (doc comment: a switch for one setting; the row around it shows the visible label, or, with `showLabel`, the switch shows its own). Destructure `showLabel = false`. The DOM, exactly:

```tsx
<span className="d-toggle">
  {showLabel ? <span id={`${id}-label`} className="d-toggle__label">{label}</span> : null}
  <button id={id} type="button" role="switch" className="d-toggle__switch" aria-checked={checked}
    aria-label={showLabel ? undefined : label} aria-labelledby={showLabel ? `${id}-label` : undefined}
    aria-describedby={hint ? `${id}-hint` : undefined} aria-disabled={disabled ? true : undefined}
    onClick={/* nothing when disabled, else onChange(!checked) */}>
    <span className="d-toggle__track" aria-hidden="true"><span className="d-toggle__knob" /></span>
  </button>
  {hint ? <span id={`${id}-hint`} className="d-toggle__hint">{hint}</span> : null}
</span>
```

`Space` and `Enter` reach `onClick` through the native button; no key handler is added. The visible label is plain text and takes no click (the switch is the one target; its 2.75rem box already meets WCAG 2.5.8). `Toggle.css`:

```css
.d-toggle__track { position: relative; display: block; width: 2.25rem; height: 1.25rem; background: var(--bg); border: 1px solid var(--edge); border-radius: var(--r-pill); transition: background var(--duration-fast), border-color var(--duration-fast); }
.d-toggle__knob { position: absolute; top: 0.1875rem; left: 0.1875rem; width: 0.75rem; height: 0.75rem; background: var(--fg-2); border-radius: var(--r-pill); transition: transform var(--duration-fast), background var(--duration-fast); }
```

`Segmented.tsx` (doc comment: a single choice among a few options, the ARIA radio group with selection following focus). Hold one ref per option button (`useRef<(HTMLButtonElement | null)[]>([])`). `checkedIndex = options.findIndex(o => o.value === value)`; `stop = checkedIndex >= 0 ? checkedIndex : 0`. The DOM, exactly:

```tsx
<div className="d-segmented">
  <span id={`${id}-label`} className="d-sr-only">{label}</span>
  <div id={id} role="radiogroup" aria-labelledby={`${id}-label`} className="d-segmented__group" onKeyDown={/* below */}>
    {options.map((o, i) => (
      <button key={o.value} ref={/* refs.current[i] */} type="button" role="radio" className="d-segmented__option"
        aria-checked={o.value === value} tabIndex={i === stop ? 0 : -1} onClick={() => onChange(o.value)}>{o.label}</button>
    ))}
  </div>
</div>
```

`onKeyDown`: `from` is the index of `event.target` among the refs (return when it is not one of them); `next = arrowIndex(event, from, options.length, 'both')`; `null` → return without `preventDefault`; else `preventDefault()`, focus `refs.current[next]`, and call `onChange(options[next].value)` when it differs from `value`. `Segmented.css`:

`SettingsFrame.tsx` (doc comment: the Settings modal of the Mesh brief, 960×640 with a 220px navigation, a native `<dialog>` so the browser traps focus and returns it). `ref = useRef<HTMLDialogElement>(null)`, `titleRef = useRef<HTMLHeadingElement>(null)`, `titleId = useId()`. Effect on `[open]`, in this order: no element → return; `open && !el.open` → `el.showModal()` then `titleRef.current?.focus()`; `!open && el.open` → `el.close()`. A second effect with `[]` returns a cleanup that calls `close()` when the element is still open (focus is handed back when the frame is torn down open). The DOM, exactly:

```tsx
<dialog ref={ref} className="d-settings-frame" aria-labelledby={titleId} aria-modal="true"
  onCancel={e => { e.preventDefault(); onClose(); }}
  onKeyDown={e => { if (e.key === 'Escape') { e.preventDefault(); onClose(); } }}
  onClick={e => { if (e.target === ref.current) onClose(); }}>
  {open ? (
    <div className="d-settings-frame__panel" onClick={e => e.stopPropagation()}>
      <div className="d-settings-frame__side">
        <h1 ref={titleRef} id={titleId} tabIndex={-1} className="d-settings-frame__title">{title}</h1>
        {nav}
      </div>
      <div className="d-settings-frame__pane">
        <div className="d-settings-frame__bar"><Button variant="ghost" keyHint="esc" onClick={onClose}>{closeLabel}</Button></div>
        <div className="d-settings-frame__body">{children}</div>
      </div>
    </div>
  ) : null}
</dialog>
```

```tsx
import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite';
import { SettingsFrame } from './SettingsFrame.tsx';
import { SettingsNav } from '../SettingsNav/SettingsNav.tsx';
import { SettingsRow } from '../SettingsRow/SettingsRow.tsx';
import { Segmented } from '../Segmented/Segmented.tsx';
import { Toggle } from '../Toggle/Toggle.tsx';
import { DeviceRow } from '../DeviceRow/DeviceRow.tsx';
import { Button } from '../Button/Button.tsx';

// Every string is L-COPY-02's (settings.*, devices.*, notify.*). The composed Screens/Settings stories of
// task 19 quote en.ts; these show the frame itself.
const meta: Meta = { title: 'Settings/SettingsFrame', parameters: { layout: 'fullscreen' } };
export default meta;
type Story = StoryObj;
const noop = () => {};
const ITEMS = [{ id: 'devices', label: 'devices' }, { id: 'notifications', label: 'notifications' }, { id: 'appearance', label: 'appearance' }];
const NOTIFY = [{ value: 'dms-mentions', label: 'direct messages and mentions' }, { value: 'everything', label: 'every message' }, { value: 'nothing', label: 'nothing' }];
const MODES = [{ value: 'default', label: 'default' }, { value: 'all', label: 'all' }, { value: 'mentions', label: 'mentions' }, { value: 'nothing', label: 'nothing' }];
const remove = { label: 'remove', onAction: noop };

function DevicesSection() {
  return (
    <section aria-labelledby="devices-title">
      <h2 id="devices-title">Devices</h2>
      <p>Every browser and app signed in to your account. Removing a device needs your recovery key.</p>
      <ul role="list" style={{ listStyle: 'none', margin: 0, padding: 0 }}>
        <DeviceRow name="3f9a2c1d" tier="web" tierLabel="browser" own ownLabel="this browser" lastSeen="last seen 21:04" />
        <DeviceRow name="b2d4e6f8" tier="native" tierLabel="app" lastSeen="last seen 21:02" action={remove} />
        <DeviceRow name="0a1b2c3d" tier="web" tierLabel="browser" state="not yet in the device list" lastSeen="last seen 20:40" action={remove} />
        <DeviceRow name="99ee0f11" tier="web" tierLabel="browser" state="removed" lastSeen="last seen 1 Oct 2026" />
      </ul>
      <div style={{ display: 'flex', flexWrap: 'wrap', alignItems: 'center', justifyContent: 'space-between', gap: '0.75rem', padding: '0.75rem 0' }}>
        <span>3 devices</span>
        <Button>refresh</Button>
      </div>
      <div style={{ display: 'flex', flexWrap: 'wrap', gap: '0.5rem', paddingTop: '0.75rem', borderTop: '1px solid var(--hairline)' }}>
        <Button variant="danger">Sign out and remove this browser</Button>
        <Button>Forget this browser</Button>
      </div>
    </section>
  );
}

function NotificationsSection() {
  return (
    <section aria-labelledby="notify-title">
      <h2 id="notify-title">Notifications</h2>
      <p>Desktop notifications show while a dilla tab is open. Nothing is shown when every tab is closed.</p>
      <SettingsRow id="notify-permission" label="Desktop notifications"><Button variant="accent">Turn on</Button></SettingsRow>
      <SettingsRow id="notify-default" label="Notify me about">
        <Segmented id="notify-default-control" label="Notify me about" options={NOTIFY} value="dms-mentions" onChange={noop} />
      </SettingsRow>
      <h3>Per channel</h3>
      <p>Every channel and direct message. Rows left on default follow the choice above.</p>
      <SettingsRow id="notify-general" label="#general · Midgard Crew">
        <div style={{ display: 'flex', flexWrap: 'wrap', alignItems: 'center', gap: '0.75rem' }}>
          <Segmented id="notify-general-mode" label="#general · Midgard Crew" options={MODES} value="all" onChange={noop} />
          <Toggle id="mute-general" label="mute" checked={false} onChange={noop} showLabel />
        </div>
      </SettingsRow>
      <SettingsRow id="notify-random" label="#random · Midgard Crew">
        <div style={{ display: 'flex', flexWrap: 'wrap', alignItems: 'center', gap: '0.75rem' }}>
          <Segmented id="notify-random-mode" label="#random · Midgard Crew" options={MODES} value="nothing" onChange={noop} />
          <Toggle id="mute-random" label="mute" checked onChange={noop} showLabel />
        </div>
      </SettingsRow>
      <SettingsRow id="notify-ada" label="ada">
        <div style={{ display: 'flex', flexWrap: 'wrap', alignItems: 'center', gap: '0.75rem' }}>
          <Segmented id="notify-ada-mode" label="ada" options={MODES} value="default" onChange={noop} />
          <Toggle id="mute-ada" label="mute" checked={false} onChange={noop} showLabel />
        </div>
      </SettingsRow>
    </section>
  );
}

function Frame({ section }: { section: 'devices' | 'notifications' }) {
  return (
    <SettingsFrame open title="Settings" closeLabel="Close settings" onClose={noop}
      nav={<SettingsNav label="settings sections" items={ITEMS} activeId={section} onSelect={noop} />}>
      {section === 'devices' ? <DevicesSection /> : <NotificationsSection />}
    </SettingsFrame>
  );
}

export const Devices: Story = { render: () => <Frame section="devices" /> };
export const Notifications: Story = { render: () => <Frame section="notifications" /> };
// 360 × 740 through the frame's own size variables: the container query stacks the navigation.
export const Narrow: Story = {
  render: () => <div style={{ ['--d-settings-w' as string]: '22.5rem', ['--d-settings-h' as string]: '46.25rem' }}><Frame section="devices" /></div>,
};
```

  - Global Constraints "Accessibility rules": the sidebar `tablist` before the list as one tab stop with `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight`; the rail's last item is the settings button inside the roving group; a `Pill` in a row or rail item is decorative for assistive technology and the row's accessible name carries the count in words through `aria-label`; a muted row says so. Ruling 15: a muted channel hides its unread count, its mention count still shows. Brief "Removed from the chrome": no pill on an empty channel or DM.
- Produces (exactly):
  ```ts
  // L-UI-27  packages/ui/src/SidebarTabs/SidebarTabs.tsx
  export interface SidebarTabsProps { label: string; tabs: readonly { id: string; label: string; count?: number; mentions?: number }[]; activeId: string; onSelect(id: string): void; }
  export function SidebarTabs(props: SidebarTabsProps): React.JSX.Element;   // inferred in code, not annotated, as every component of the package
  // L-UI-28  packages/ui/src/ChannelList/ChannelList.tsx (amends web-1 L-UI-09)
  export interface ChannelListProps { label: string; title: string;
    channels: readonly { id: string; name: string; kind: 'text' | 'voice' | 'dm'; readable: boolean; unread?: number; mentions?: number; muted?: boolean }[];
    activeId: string | null; onSelect(id: string): void; emptyLabel: string; rowLabel?(c: { name: string; unread: number; mentions: number; muted: boolean }): string;
    tabs?: ReactNode; footer?: ReactNode;
  }
  // L-UI-29  packages/ui/src/CommunityRail/CommunityRail.tsx (amends web-1 L-UI-08)
  export interface CommunityRailProps { label: string; items: readonly { id: string; name: string; unread?: number; mentions?: number }[]; activeId: string | null; onSelect(id: string): void;
    joinLabel: string; onJoin(): void; settingsLabel?: string; onSettings?(): void; itemLabel?(i: { name: string; unread: number; mentions: number }): string; }
  // packages/ui/src/ChannelRow/ChannelRow.tsx (the pre-web-1 primitive)
  export type ChannelRowProps = {
    name: string; kind: 'text' | 'voice' | 'dm'; active?: boolean; unread?: number; mentions?: number;
    muted?: boolean; readable?: boolean; private?: boolean; onSelect: () => void;
    ariaLabel?: string;
  };
  // L-UI-30  packages/ui/src/ChannelHeader/ChannelHeader.tsx (amends web-1)
  export interface ChannelHeaderProps { name: string; topic?: string; readable?: boolean; readableLabel?: string; kind?: 'channel' | 'dm'; }
  ```
  `index.ts` exports `SidebarTabs` and `SidebarTabsProps` (`ChannelHeader` and its props type are exported already). DOM contract (tasks 20, 22 rely on it): `SidebarTabs` is `<div role="tablist" aria-label class="d-sidebar-tabs">` of `<button type="button" role="tab" aria-selected>` named by their label (plus the pill's words when a count shows; a test locates a tab by substring, never `exact: true`), each with `data-count` (the `count`, `"0"` when absent) and `data-mentions`; every `ChannelRow` button carries `data-kind` (`text|voice|dm`), `data-unread` (the unread count the row **shows**, a decimal string: `"0"` when muted or quiet), `data-mentions` (the mention count, decimal) and `data-muted="true"` when muted; every rail item button carries `data-unread` and `data-mentions` (decimal, `"0"` when absent); the rail's settings control is `<button aria-label={settingsLabel}>`, the last item of the rail's one roving group; with `tabs`, `ChannelList` renders `nav > h1, tabs, div[role=tabpanel][aria-label=label] > ul (or the empty label), then div.d-channel-list__footer when footer is given`; a quiet row's accessible name is its bare name, a row with something to report is named by `rowLabel`'s string; `ChannelHeader` with `kind="dm"` draws `[ @ name ]` and its heading is named by the name alone.

**Requirements:**
1. `SidebarTabs` (L-UI-27; brief "Layout": tabs CHANNELS / DMS; Mesh `mesh-chrome.css:413-433`): one `<button type="button" role="tab">` per entry in order inside `role="tablist"` named by `label`; `aria-selected="true"` on the entry whose `id` is `activeId`; one tab stop (the selected tab `tabIndex=0`, the others `-1`; the first when none matches); `ArrowRight` and `ArrowLeft` move to the next or previous tab, wrapping, `Home`/`End` to the ends, each focusing the tab and calling `onSelect(id)` when it is not already active (selection follows focus: the panel shows at once, the APG automatic-activation pattern); `ArrowUp`, `ArrowDown` and modified keys are left alone; a click, `Enter` or `Space` calls `onSelect(id)`. A tab with `mentions > 0` shows a mention `Pill` with that count; else with `count > 0` an unread `Pill`; else none (brief: no pill on empty). The selected tab is marked by an accent underline bar (`box-shadow`) as well as colour. Each tab is at least 2.25rem tall.
2. `ChannelRow` (L-UI-28 and the comment under it): `kind` accepts `'dm'`, drawn with a 0.5rem dot in the glyph column (`aria-hidden`; one row height, L-UI-30) instead of `#`/`♪`; `ariaLabel`, when given, is the button's `aria-label`; the shown unread count is `muted ? 0 : unread`; the mention pill shows when `mentions > 0`, else the unread pill when the shown unread count is above 0, else none; `data-unread` is the shown count and `data-mentions` the mention count, both always present as decimal strings; `data-muted="true"` when muted. A row with a shown count or mentions is bold (`--fg`, 700); a muted row dims its glyph and name only, so the pill keeps full contrast (brief:122-123; ruling 15). Long names (DMs list member names) are cut with an ellipsis.
3. `ChannelList` (L-UI-28): passes `unread`, `mentions` and `muted` (absent → 0, 0, false) to every row; `ariaLabel = rowLabel({ name, unread, mentions, muted })` when `rowLabel` is given **and** the row has something to report (`unread > 0 || mentions > 0 || muted`), else none (the name alone; ruling 34); `rowLabel` receives the real counts (a muted row's `unread` too). When `tabs` is given it is rendered between the `<h1>` and the list, and the list (or the empty label) sits inside `<div role="tabpanel" aria-label={label} class="d-channel-list__panel">`; without `tabs` the DOM is web-1's. When `footer` is given it is rendered as `<div class="d-channel-list__footer">{footer}</div>` after the list or after the empty label: inside the `tabpanel` when `tabs` is given, else directly inside the `nav`; without `footer` nothing more renders. The footer sits outside the roving `ul`, so its control is its own tab stop after the rows. Roving focus over the rows is unchanged.
3a. `ChannelHeader` (L-UI-30, ruling 36): `kind` defaults to `'channel'`; `kind="dm"` draws the glyph `@` in place of `#` inside the same bracket (`[ @ name ]`), the bracket spans `aria-hidden` as today, so the heading is named by the name alone; nothing else changes (topic, readable glyph, no focusable element).
4. `CommunityRail` (L-UI-29): each item button carries `data-unread` and `data-mentions` (decimal strings, absent → `"0"`) and shows the mention `Pill` when `mentions > 0`, else the unread `Pill` when `unread > 0`, at the tile's top-right corner over a ring of the rail's background; `aria-label = itemLabel({ name, unread, mentions })` when `itemLabel` is given and `unread > 0 || mentions > 0`, else the web-1 name (`d-sr-only` name plus the pill's words). When **both** `settingsLabel` and `onSettings` are given, one more `<li>` after the join tile holds `<button type="button" aria-label={settingsLabel}>` with the Mesh cog drawn as an `aria-hidden` inline SVG in `currentColor`, inside the same roving `ul` (so `End` reaches it and Tab does not stop on it separately), visually separated from the servers by a hairline; it calls `onSettings` on click, `Enter` and `Space`. Tiles stay 2.5rem square (40 × 40, brief "Layout").
5. The composed shell fixture (`AppShell.fixture.tsx`, used by the `Shell/AppShell` stories and the focus-order test) shows the tabs, badges on rows and rail items, a muted row, the rail's settings button and, on the DMs tab, the footer button `message someone`; the focus order of the keyboard map becomes skip link → rail (one stop) → sidebar tabs (one stop) → channel rows (one stop) → log → composer → send → status bar.
6. Tokens only; three themes; reduced motion (no transition); `vitest-axe` with no serious or critical violation; the Storybook test-runner's axe (with `target-size`, the `Shell/` titles are already strict) and focus-ring checks pass for every story (Global Constraints "Accessibility rules").
7. Stories: `Shell/SidebarTabs` (Channels, DirectMessages, Quiet), `Shell/ChannelList` gains Badges, DirectMessages (with the `footer` ghost button `message someone`), WithTabs, `Shell/CommunityRail` gains Badges, WithSettings, `Shell/ChannelHeader` gains DirectMessage, `Primitives/ChannelRow` gains DirectMessage, MutedWithMention; the `Shell/AppShell` stories show the new fixture. Screenshots of every `shell-` story and every `primitives-channelrow--` story in three themes: 30 stories, 90 PNGs under `target/ui-screens/web-2a/` (F16).
8. No word `scripts/check-ui-copy.mjs:5-11` forbids in any new literal. Lesson (e): no refusal is added. Lessons (c), (d), (f), (g): not applicable (no browser e2e, server behaviour or store).

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';
import userEvent from '@testing-library/user-event';
import { describe, it, expect, vi } from 'vitest';
import { SidebarTabs, type SidebarTabsProps } from './SidebarTabs.tsx';
import { expectNoAxeViolations } from '../test/setup.ts';

// L-COPY-02: shell.tabs.label, shell.tabs.channels, shell.tabs.dms.
type Tabs = SidebarTabsProps['tabs'];
const QUIET: Tabs = [{ id: 'channels', label: 'channels' }, { id: 'dms', label: 'direct messages' }];

function Controlled({ tabs = QUIET, onValue }: { tabs?: Tabs; onValue?: (id: string) => void }) {
  const [active, setActive] = useState('channels');
  return (
    <>
      <button type="button">before</button>
      <SidebarTabs label="sidebar" tabs={tabs} activeId={active} onSelect={id => { setActive(id); onValue?.(id); }} />
      <button type="button">after</button>
    </>
  );
}
const tab = (name: string) => screen.getByRole('tab', { name });

describe('SidebarTabs', () => {
  it('is a tablist named by its label, one tab button per entry, the active one selected', () => {
    const { container } = render(<SidebarTabs label="sidebar" tabs={QUIET} activeId="dms" onSelect={() => {}} />);
    const list = screen.getByRole('tablist', { name: 'sidebar' });
    expect(container.firstElementChild).toBe(list);
    expect(list).toHaveClass('d-sidebar-tabs');
    const tabs = screen.getAllByRole('tab');
    expect(tabs.map(t => t.tagName)).toEqual(['BUTTON', 'BUTTON']);
    expect(tabs.map(t => t.textContent)).toEqual(['channels', 'direct messages']);
    expect(tabs.map(t => t.getAttribute('aria-selected'))).toEqual(['false', 'true']);
    expect(tabs.map(t => t.getAttribute('data-count'))).toEqual(['0', '0']);
  });

  it('is one tab stop, on the selected tab', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    render(<Controlled />);
    await user.tab();
    await user.tab();
    expect(tab('channels')).toHaveFocus();
    await user.tab();
    expect(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'after' })).toHaveFocus();
    await user.tab({ shift: true });
    expect(tab('channels')).toHaveFocus();
  });

  it('moves and selects with ArrowLeft and ArrowRight, wrapping, and with Home and End', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const onValue = vi.fn();
    render(<Controlled onValue={onValue} />);
    await user.tab();
    await user.tab();
    await user.keyboard('{ArrowRight}');
    expect(tab('direct messages')).toHaveFocus();
    expect(tab('direct messages')).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'true');
    await user.keyboard('{ArrowRight}');
    expect(tab('channels')).toHaveFocus();
    await user.keyboard('{ArrowLeft}');

  });

  it('leaves ArrowUp, ArrowDown and modified arrows alone, and selects on click', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const onValue = vi.fn();
    render(<Controlled onValue={onValue} />);
    await user.tab();
    await user.tab();
    await user.keyboard('{ArrowDown}{ArrowUp}{Alt>}{ArrowRight}{/Alt}');
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement `SidebarTabs`, the `ChannelRow` changes and the `ChannelHeader` kind**

`SidebarTabs.tsx` (doc comment: the sidebar's channels / direct messages switch, the Mesh tabs; selection follows focus). Hold one ref per tab button. `activeIndex = tabs.findIndex(t => t.id === activeId)`, `stop = activeIndex >= 0 ? activeIndex : 0`. The DOM, exactly:

```tsx
<div className="d-sidebar-tabs" role="tablist" aria-label={label} onKeyDown={/* below */}>
  {tabs.map((t, i) => (
    <button key={t.id} ref={/* refs.current[i] */} type="button" role="tab" className="d-sidebar-tabs__tab"
      aria-selected={t.id === activeId} tabIndex={i === stop ? 0 : -1}
      data-count={String(t.count ?? 0)} data-mentions={String(t.mentions ?? 0)} onClick={() => onSelect(t.id)}>
      <span className="d-sidebar-tabs__label">{t.label}</span>
      {(t.mentions ?? 0) > 0 ? <Pill kind="mention" count={t.mentions ?? 0} /> : (t.count ?? 0) > 0 ? <Pill kind="unread" count={t.count ?? 0} /> : null}
    </button>
  ))}
</div>
```

`onKeyDown`: `from` = index of `event.target` among the refs (return when none); `next = arrowIndex(event, from, tabs.length, 'horizontal')`; `null` → return; else `preventDefault()`, focus `refs.current[next]`, and `onSelect(tabs[next].id)` when it is not `activeId`. `SidebarTabs.css` (the uppercase is on the label only, so a screen reader never meets transformed count words):

```css

.d-sidebar-tabs__label { font-size: var(--text-micro); font-weight: var(--weight-label); letter-spacing: var(--label-tracking); text-transform: uppercase; }
.d-sidebar-tabs__tab:hover { color: var(--fg); }
.d-sidebar-tabs__tab[aria-selected="true"] { color: var(--accent); box-shadow: inset 0 -2px 0 var(--accent); }
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .d-sidebar-tabs__tab { transition: none; } }
```

**Interfaces:**

Consumes:
- **L-TS-23** (task 14), exactly:
  ```ts
  export type Command = /* the web-1 thirteen */
    | { m: 'signInBegin' }                                         // needs-signup → signin-login
    | { m: 'signInLogin'; username: string; password: string }     // signin-login → signin-totp | signin-key
    | { m: 'signInTotp'; code: string }                            // signin-totp → signin-key
    | { m: 'signInKey'; recoveryKey: string }                      // signin-key → ready
    | { m: 'signInCancel' }                                        // signin-* → needs-signup
    /* … the seven ready commands, consumed by tasks 19 and 20 */;
  export type BootPhase = /* web-1 ten */ | 'signin-login' | 'signin-totp' | 'signin-key' | 'enrolling' | 'cleared';
  ```
  Results: `signInLogin` → `{ needsTotp: boolean }`, every other sign-in command → `null`. Error codes the
  worker adds: `E_NO_BACKUP`, `E_LIST_RACE`, `E_RECOVERY_KEY`, `E_DEVICE_UNLISTED`, `E_SETTING_KEY`,
  `E_NO_ASSERTION`, and `E_ENROL_RATE` (status 429, `retryAfterMs` kept: a 429 raised inside `Enrol.register`,
  the per-user enrolment rate or the challenge's network rate; the login route's 429 stays `E_RATE_LIMITED`,
  ruling 38). `ACCEPTS`: `needs-signup` adds `signInBegin`; `signin-login` accepts `signInLogin`,
  `signInCancel`; `signin-totp` accepts `signInTotp`, `signInCancel`; `signin-key` accepts `signInKey`,
  `signInCancel`; `enrolling` and `cleared` accept nothing but `start`. A refused `signInLogin` publishes
  `account.error` and stays in `signin-login`; a rejection of `Enrol.totp` (and `E_NO_ASSERTION`) sets the phase
  `signin-login` with `signIn.username` kept (ruling 39); a rejection of `Enrol.register` (after the login or
  after the code) ends in `signin-login` with the error; a missing backup **rejects** the command with
  `E_NO_BACKUP` **and** leaves the phase at `signin-key` with `account.error.code === 'E_NO_BACKUP'`;
  `E_RECOVERY_KEY` returns to `signin-key`; `E_LIST_RACE` wipes the store and ends in `cleared` with
  `account.error.code === 'E_LIST_RACE'` (ruling 26); a boot in core phase 3 with a recorded user lands in
  `signin-key` (after `Enrol.fetch`, so `E_NO_BACKUP` can be the account error there too).
- **L-TS-27** (head; this task makes the `welcome` change and the `cleared` reload, task 19 the rest):
  `{ name: 'welcome'; invite: string | null; signin: 'race' | null }` read from `/welcome[?invite=…][&signin=race]`;
  `App.screenFor('cleared')` is `'boot'` and an effect in `App` calls
  `reload(account.error?.code === 'E_LIST_RACE' ? '/welcome?signin=race' : '/')` once, through an injectable

- **L-TS-24** (task 14): `AccountState` gains `signIn: { username: string | null; needsTotp: boolean } | null`

- **L-CORE-28's TS twin** (task 11), exported from the package root:
  `export function normaliseRecoveryKey(text: string): string` — drops ASCII space, tab, newline, carriage

**Requirements:**

1. Four steps, each an `OnboardingFrame` whose `stepLabel` is `signin.step` with `n` = 1 (login), 2 (second
   factor), 3 (recovery key), 4 (done); an account without TOTP goes 1 → 3 → 4 (L-COPY-02 flow rules;
   ruling 16). The step shown is derived from the phase: `signin-login` → 1, `signin-totp` → 2, `signin-key`
   and `enrolling` → 3, `ready` after this mount's `signInKey` resolved → 4. A phase of `ready` reached in any
   other way (the account was ready before this screen mounted) shows step 4 as well (the App never mounts
   this screen then; the rule only keeps the screen total). The step never follows the command the page sent:
   a refusal that moves the phase (a refused code → `signin-login`) shows the step of the new phase. The App
   never mounts this screen in `cleared` (requirement 13).
2. Steps 1–3 are each one `<form noValidate>` whose forward button is `type="submit"`; `Cancel` and
   `Create a new account instead` are `type="button"` and send `{ m: 'signInCancel' }` (flow rules). Step 1's
   footer is `[Create a new account instead (ghost)] [Continue (accent)]`; steps 2 and 3:
   `[Cancel (ghost)] [Continue | Add this browser (accent)]`; step 4: `[Open dilla (accent)]`, `type="button"`,
   calling `props.onFinish()`.
3. Step 1 (login): `signin.login.title` with `{instance}` = `account.instance.name`, `signin.login.body`, a
   `TextField` `Username` (`id="signin-username"`, `autoComplete="username"`, `spellCheck={false}`,
   `required`, `maxLength={32}`, initial value `account.signIn?.username ?? ''`) and a `TextField` `Password`
   (`id="signin-password"`, `type="password"`, `autoComplete="current-password"`, `required`). Submit: when the
   trimmed username or the password is empty, each empty field shows the field error `signin.error.required`
   (`Fill in this field.`), focus moves to the first empty field (username before password), nothing is sent,
   and the fields keep their `required` attribute; otherwise `{ m: 'signInLogin', username: username.trim().toLowerCase(), password }` (the same case mapping
   as signup, `Onboarding.tsx:197`, `internal/auth/handle.go`). While it is in flight the forward button reads
   `signin.login.working`, both footer buttons carry `aria-disabled="true"` and keep focus, and a second submit
   sends nothing. On success the password state is set to `''` (the password stays in page memory no longer
   than the call: Global Constraints "Never written").
4. Step 2 (second factor): `signin.totp.title`, `signin.totp.body`, a `TextField` `Code` (`id="signin-code"`,
   `inputMode="numeric"`, `autoComplete="one-time-code"`, `spellCheck={false}`, `maxLength={6}`, `required`).
   Submit with an empty trimmed code shows the field error `signin.error.required`, sends nothing and focuses
   the field; otherwise
   `{ m: 'signInTotp', code: code.trim() }`, busy exactly as step 1 (label `signin.login.working`).
5. Step 3 (recovery key): `signin.key.title`, `signin.key.body`, a `RecoveryKeyField` `Recovery key`
   (`id="signin-key"`) whose `hint` is `signin.key.hint` with `n = normaliseRecoveryKey(value).length`, paste
   allowed (F2, WCAG 3.3.8). While `n !== 52` the forward button `Add this browser` carries
   `aria-disabled="true"` and `aria-describedby="signin-key-length"`, and a paragraph
   `<p id="signin-key-length">` holding `signin.error.keyLength` is rendered after the field (the onboarding
   acknowledgement pattern, `Onboarding.tsx:297-308`). A submit while `n !== 52` sends nothing, sets the
   field's `error` to `signin.error.keyLength` and focuses the field. With `n === 52` the submit sends
   `{ m: 'signInKey', recoveryKey: value }` — the **raw** text as typed or pasted (Rust normalises,
   L-CORE-26 step 1; the page never sends a second, different spelling). On success the key state is set to
   `''`.
6. `enrolling` (and the in-flight `signInKey`): step 3 stays, the field keeps its text and focus, a
   `<p role="status">` holds `signin.key.working`, `Add this browser` and `Cancel` carry `aria-disabled="true"`,
   every submit and every cancel sends nothing (`enrolling` accepts nothing, L-TS-23).
7. Step 4 (done): `signin.done.title`; `signin.done.body` with `{username}` = `account.user?.username ??
   account.signIn?.username ?? username.trim().toLowerCase()` and `{instance}`; `signin.done.next`.
8. Focus (flow 01's rules, Global Constraints Accessibility): every change of the shown step moves focus to
   its `<h1>` (the frame does it on a title change); a refusal that names a field moves focus to that field
   after the frame's heading focus (the `focusRequest` effect pattern of `Onboarding.tsx:119-124`, which runs
   after the child frame's effect); a refusal shown as a banner leaves focus where it is (on the pressed
   button) unless its row names a focus target, and the `Banner` is the first child of the step body
   (`role="alert"` announces it).
9. The step rendered follows `account.phase`, never the command sent (L-COPY-02 flow rules): a banner is
   attached to the step the phase names, so a refusal after which the worker moved the phase to `signin-login`
   shows its banner on step 1. Refusals — switched on `code` and `status` only, never on `detail` (protocol/02;
   copy rules) — are mapped by one function `signInRefusal(e: UiError, command: 'login' | 'totp' | 'key',
   instance: string)` in this order of tests, the first that matches wins:

   | test on `e` | shown | where |
   |---|---|---|
   | `code === 'E_NO_BACKUP'` | danger banner `signin.error.noBackup` `{instance}` | step 3 with no field and no forward button: `Cancel` is the only control |
   | `code === 'E_RECOVERY_KEY'` | field error `signin.error.wrongKey` | the recovery-key field keeps its text; focus to the field |
   | `(code === 'E_UNAUTHENTICATED' \|\| code === 'E_NO_ASSERTION') && command === 'totp'` | warn banner `signin.error.totpFailed` | **step 1** (the worker moved the phase to `signin-login`; the assertion is spent, ruling 39): the username field keeps its text, the password field is empty and receives focus |
   | `code === 'E_UNAUTHENTICATED' && command === 'login'` | field error `signin.error.loginFailed` | the password field; focus to it |
   | `code === 'E_FORBIDDEN' && command !== 'key'` | danger banner `signin.error.deviceCap` `{instance}` | step 1 (the phase is `signin-login`: a refused login stays there, a refused registration after the code returns there; the disabled account's 403 is a race the password login already refuses, ruling 38) |
   | `code === 'E_ENROL_RATE'` | warn banner `signin.error.tooMany`, `minutes = Math.ceil(retryAfterMs / 60000)`, `60` when `retryAfterMs` is null | step 1 (the worker produces the code for a 429 inside `Enrol.register` and ends in `signin-login`, L-TS-23) |
   | `code === 'E_RATE_LIMITED'` | warn banner `signin.error.rateLimited`, `seconds = Math.ceil(retryAfterMs / 1000)`; `onboarding.error.rateLimitedNoWait` when `retryAfterMs` is null | stays |
   | `code === 'E_NETWORK' \|\| status >= 500` | danger banner `signin.error.network` | stays |
   | anything else | danger banner `signin.error.other` `{code}` | stays |

   `E_LIST_RACE` has no row: the worker answers it with the wipe and the `cleared` phase, the App replaces this
   screen with the `Boot` splash and reloads to `/welcome?signin=race`, and `Onboarding` shows
   `signin.error.listRace` there (requirements 12 and 13; ruling 26). The command's rejection still reaches
   `apply` and maps to the last row, but the screen is unmounted by then and nothing of it is seen.
   Every new submit clears the banner and the field errors first; editing a field clears that field's error.
   **Attacker statement (lesson e):** this screen adds no refusal of its own; the required-field and
   52-character gates are tripped only by the person typing, and they send nothing rather than refuse
   anything. Every row above shows a refusal the worker or the server made.
10. `E_NO_BACKUP` is also read from the account slice: when the phase is `signin-key`, no call of this mount is
    in flight and `account.error?.code === 'E_NO_BACKUP'`, the no-backup view of row 1 is shown (a reload in
    the ceremony, L-TS-23 "Boot with identity().phase === 3"). This is the plan, not a fallback: L-TS-23 says
    `Enrol.fetch`'s failure rejects the command **and** leaves the error in the slice, and the screen handles
    both. No other code is read from `account.error`.
11. While `account` is `undefined` or `account.instance` is `null`, the screen is the loading `Splash`
    (`boot.loading.status`), as `Onboarding.tsx:126`.
12. Onboarding's entry: on step 1 (connect), below the invite field and inside the form body, a
    `Button variant="ghost" type="button"` `onboarding.connect.signIn`, rendered only when
    `instance.passwordSignup` is true (ruling 22). Its click sends `{ m: 'signInBegin' }`; while in flight it
    carries `aria-disabled="true"` and a second click sends nothing; a refusal shows the danger banner
    `signin.error.other` `{code}` on step 1. The same entry (same rules) is rendered on the closed frame
    (`registrationMode === 2`) below its body text (L-COPY-02 flow rules: an existing account on a closed
    instance must still be able to add a browser); the closed frame also renders the banner slot as the first
    child of its body, so the entry's refusal and the race banner of requirement 12b show there too. It never
    appears on steps 2–5.
12b. The race banner (L-TS-27, ruling 26): when `Onboarding` mounts on `{ name: 'welcome', signin: 'race' }`,
    its `banner` state starts as the warn banner `signin.error.listRace` (no variables, no reload action),
    shown above the form on the connect step (and on the closed frame). Its first navigation away — the connect
    step's successful `connectNext` (before `goTo('identity')`) or the entry's `beginSignIn` (before the
    command is sent) — writes the route without `signin`:
    `navigate({ name: 'welcome', invite: route.invite, signin: null }, true)`, and the banner is dropped by the
    `setBanner(null)` both already do. A route without `signin=race` never shows it; the query is the only
    place the message survives the reload the wipe forces.
13. App: `screenFor` returns `'signin'` for `signin-login`, `signin-totp`, `signin-key`, `enrolling`, and
    `'boot'` for `cleared` (an explicit case, so the `Boot` splash `Starting dilla` shows while the page
    reloads). `App` keeps a `signingIn` hold like the onboarding hold (`App.tsx:36-38`): set when the screen is
    `'signin'`, cleared when the screen is `'onboarding'` (a cancelled sign-in) and by the done step's
    `onFinish`; and the screen `'signin'` clears the onboarding hold. `SignIn` is rendered when the screen is
    `'signin'`, or when `signingIn` holds and the phase is `ready` (never in `cleared`). `onFinish` navigates

```tsx
import { describe, it, expect, vi } from 'vitest';
import { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';
import userEvent, { type UserEvent } from '@testing-library/user-event';
import type { AccountState, BootPhase, Command } from '@dilla/client-core';
import { CoreProvider } from '../core/context.tsx';
import { FakeClient, refusal } from '../test/fake-client.ts';
import { account, INSTANCE } from '../test/fixtures.ts';
import { expectNoAxeViolations } from '../test/setup.ts';
import { SignIn } from './SignIn.tsx';

const KEY = '7K2MQX9DH4TBR8NWC3VFJ6PZA1GEY5KSM0QTB7XHW2DNF9RCP4ZA';
const GROUPED = '7K2M-QX9D-H4TB-R8NW-C3VF-J6PZ-A1GE-Y5KS-M0QT-B7XH-W2DN-F9RC-P4ZA';
const ME = { id: 'bb'.repeat(16), username: 'ada' };
const LENGTH = 'A recovery key has 52 characters.';
type Script = (c: Command, fake: FakeClient) => Promise<unknown>;
const idle: Script = () => Promise.resolve(null);

function move(fake: FakeClient, over: Partial<AccountState>): void {
  const current = fake.get('account');
  if (current === undefined) throw new Error('no account slice');
  fake.set('account', { ...current, ...over });
}
function setup(phase: BootPhase, script: Script = idle, over: Partial<AccountState> = {}) {
  const fake = new FakeClient();
  fake.set('account', account({
    phase, user: null, deviceId: null, instance: { ...INSTANCE, passwordSignup: true },
    signIn: { username: null, needsTotp: false }, ...over,
  }));
  fake.handler = c => script(c, fake);
  const onFinish = vi.fn();
  const user = userEvent.setup();
  const view = render(<div className="d-root"><CoreProvider client={fake}><SignIn onFinish={onFinish} /></CoreProvider></div>);
  return { fake, onFinish, user, view };
}
const h1 = () => screen.getByRole('heading', { level: 1 });
const button = (name: string) => screen.getByRole('button', { name });
const field = (name: string) => screen.getByRole('textbox', { name });
const password = () => screen.getByLabelText('Password');

/** The worker of L-TS-23 as the page sees it: login → key (or second factor) → ready. */
const worker = (opts: { totp?: boolean } = {}): Script => (c, fake) => {
  switch (c.m) {
    case 'signInLogin':
      move(fake, { phase: opts.totp ? 'signin-totp' : 'signin-key', signIn: { username: c.username, needsTotp: opts.totp === true } });
      return Promise.resolve({ needsTotp: opts.totp === true });
    case 'signInTotp':
      move(fake, { phase: 'signin-key' });
      return Promise.resolve(null);
    case 'signInKey':
      move(fake, { phase: 'ready', user: ME, deviceId: 'dd'.repeat(16), signIn: null });
      return Promise.resolve(null);
    case 'signInCancel':
      move(fake, { phase: 'needs-signup', signIn: null });
      return Promise.resolve(null);
    default:
      return Promise.resolve(null);
  }
};
async function login(user: UserEvent): Promise<void> {
  await user.type(field('Username'), ' Ada ');
  await user.type(password(), 'correct horse');
  await user.click(button('Continue'));
}
async function pasteKey(user: UserEvent, text = GROUPED): Promise<void> {
  await user.click(field('Recovery key'));
  await user.paste(text);
}
```

```tsx
describe('App sign-in', () => {
  function signInWorker(fake: FakeClient) {
    const move = (over: Partial<ReturnType<typeof account>>) => fake.set('account', { ...fake.get('account')!, ...over });
    fake.handler = c => {
      if (c.m === 'signInBegin') move({ phase: 'signin-login', signIn: { username: null, needsTotp: false } });

      if (c.m === 'signInCancel') move({ phase: 'needs-signup', signIn: null });
```

```ts
const FLOWS = join(SRC, '..', '..', '..', 'docs', 'design', 'flows');
const FLOW_FILES = ['01-onboarding.md', '02-recovery-key.md', '03-sign-in.md'] as const;
const COPY_HEADER = /^\|\s*key\s*\|\s*text\s*\|/;
const COPY_ROW = /^\|\s*`([^`]+)`\s*\|\s*`([^`]*)`\s*\|/;
// Key prefixes the flows quote before en.ts holds them: task 19 removes 'settings.' and 'devices.', task 20
// removes 'shell.' and deletes this constant.
const COPY_PENDING: readonly string[] = ['settings.', 'devices.', 'shell.'];

/** The [key, text] rows of every table in a flow document whose header starts `| key | text |`. */
export function copyRows(source: string): { rows: [string, string][]; unparsed: string[] } {
  const rows: [string, string][] = [];
  const unparsed: string[] = [];
  let inTable = false;
  for (const line of source.split('\n')) {
    if (COPY_HEADER.test(line)) { inTable = true; continue; }
    if (!inTable) continue;
    if (!line.startsWith('|')) { inTable = false; continue; }
    if (/^\|\s*-/.test(line)) continue;
    const m = COPY_ROW.exec(line);
    if (m === null) unparsed.push(line); else rows.push([m[1], m[2]]);
  }
  return { rows, unparsed };
}

describe('the flows quote en.ts', () => {
  it('reads every row of a copy table and nothing else', () => {
    const doc = [
      '| key | text | where |', '|---|---|---|', '| `a.b` | `One` | x |', '| `c.d` | `Two’s` |', '',
      '| check | where |', '|---|---|', '| `e.f` | `no` |', '',
      '| key | text |', '|---|---|', '| g.h | `x` |',
    ].join('\n');
    expect(copyRows(doc)).toEqual({ rows: [['a.b', 'One'], ['c.d', 'Two’s']], unparsed: ['| g.h | `x` |'] });
  });
  it.each(FLOW_FILES)('every Copy row of %s equals en.ts', file => {
    const table = en as Readonly<Record<string, string>>;
    const { rows, unparsed } = copyRows(readFileSync(join(FLOWS, file), 'utf8'));
    expect(unparsed, file).toEqual([]);
    expect(rows.length, file).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    const wrong = rows
      .filter(([key, text]) => !COPY_PENDING.some(p => key.startsWith(p)) && table[key] !== text)
      .map(([key]) => `${file}: ${key}`);
    expect(wrong).toEqual([]);
  });
});
```

**`packages/web/src/screens/SignIn.tsx`** (new). Imports: `useEffect`, `useRef`, `useState`, `FormEvent`,
`ReactNode` from `react`; `normaliseRecoveryKey` from `@dilla/client-core`; `Banner`, `Button`,
`OnboardingFrame`, `RecoveryKeyField`, `Splash`, `TextField` from `@dilla/ui`; `useCore`, `errorOf`/`UiError`,
`useSlice`, `t`/`StringKey`.
- Module constants: `const KEY_LENGTH = 52;`, `type Field = 'username' | 'password' | 'code' | 'key';`, the
  field ids `signin-username`, `signin-password`, `signin-code`, `signin-key`, and the length paragraph id
  `signin-key-length`.
- `signInRefusal(e, command, instance)` returns `{ field?: Field; fieldKey?: StringKey; focus?: Field; banner?: {
  tone: 'warn' | 'danger'; key: StringKey; vars: Record<string, string | number> }; noBackup?: true }` by the
  table of requirement 9, tests in that order, reading only `e.code`, `e.status`, `e.retryAfterMs`. The
  refused-code row returns `{ banner: { tone: 'warn', key: 'signin.error.totpFailed', vars: {} }, focus:
  'password' }`.
- State: `username` (initialised once from `account?.signIn?.username ?? ''`), `password`, `code`, `key`;
  `errors: Partial<Record<Field, StringKey>>`; `banner` (the view's banner or `null`); `noBackup: boolean`;
  `busy: 'login' | 'totp' | 'key' | null`; `keyDone: boolean` (set when `signInKey` resolved);
  `focusRequest: { target: 'heading' | Field; n: number }`; a `rootRef` on the wrapping `<div>`.
- The shown step: `instance === null` → the `Splash`; `phase === 'ready'` → `done`; `noBackup ||
  (phase === 'signin-key' && busy === null && account.error?.code === 'E_NO_BACKUP')` → the no-backup view;
  `signin-totp` → `totp`; `signin-key` or `enrolling` → `key`; anything else → `login`.
  (`keyDone` is kept for the App's hold: the App mounts this screen in `ready` only through the hold.)
- The focus effect is `Onboarding.tsx:119-124`'s, keyed on `[shown, focusRequest]`: `'heading'` → the root's
  `h1`, a field → `#<field id>`.
- Each submit handler first returns when `busy !== null` or the phase is `enrolling`, then clears `banner` and
  `errors`. Login: the empty-field rule of requirement 3 (`setErrors` with `signin.error.required` on each empty
  field, `requestFocus` of the first, return); `busy = 'login'`; `await client.call({ m: 'signInLogin',
  username: username.trim().toLowerCase(), password })`; on success `setPassword('')`; in `finally`
  `busy = null`. TOTP likewise (the empty code → `signin.error.required` on `code`, focus, return). The key
  submit first applies requirement 5's length rule with `normaliseRecoveryKey(key).length`, and on success
  sets `key` to `''` and `keyDone` to true. Every rejection goes through `apply(errorOf(rejection), command)`:
  `view = signInRefusal(…)`; `view.noBackup` → `setNoBackup(true)`; `view.field` → `setErrors({ [field]:
  fieldKey })` and `requestFocus(field)`; `view.focus` → `setPassword('')` when it is `'password'` (the
  password was already dropped on the login's success; this makes the rule independent of that) and
  `requestFocus(view.focus)`; `setBanner(view.banner ?? null)`. The refused-code row's focus lands on the
  password field of step 1 because the phase slice moved to `signin-login` before the rejection reached the
  page (L-TS-23 publishes the phase, then rejects), so the shown step is `login` when the focus effect runs.
- `noBackup` resets to `false` when the phase leaves `signin-key` (an effect on the phase), so a cancel and a
  fresh ceremony start clean.
- Each field's `onChange` sets its value and deletes its own key from `errors`; while `busy !== null` or the
  phase is `enrolling`, the key field's `onChange` is ignored (the text cannot change under a running
  enrolment).
- `cancel()`: returns when `busy !== null` or the phase is `enrolling`; else `client.call({ m: 'signInCancel'
  }).catch(e => apply(errorOf(e), 'login'))`.
- Rendering follows `Onboarding.tsx:233-254`: `blockedProps = { 'aria-disabled': true }` while `busy !== null`
  or the phase is `enrolling`, on both footer buttons; the banner is the first child of the frame body; the
  key step adds `aria-disabled` and `aria-describedby="signin-key-length"` to `Add this browser` while the
  count is not 52 and renders `<p id="signin-key-length">{t('signin.error.keyLength')}</p>` after the field;
  the working paragraph `<p role="status">{t('signin.key.working')}</p>` while `busy === 'key'` or the phase
  is `enrolling`. The no-backup view is `OnboardingFrame` with `signin.key.title`, step 3, the danger banner
  and the footer `[Cancel]` only. The done step is not a form.

```tsx
import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite';
import { useState, type ReactNode } from 'react';
import { OnboardingFrame } from './OnboardingFrame.tsx';
import { TextField } from '../TextField/TextField.tsx';
import { RecoveryKeyField } from '../RecoveryKeyField/RecoveryKeyField.tsx';
import { Banner } from '../Banner/Banner.tsx';
import { Button } from '../Button/Button.tsx';
// The shipped copy of @dilla/web, so the F16 screenshots show exactly what the app says.
import { t } from '../../../web/src/strings/index.ts';

const meta = { title: 'Screens/SignIn', parameters: { layout: 'fullscreen' } } satisfies Meta;
export default meta;
type Story = StoryObj<typeof meta>;

const instance = 'dilla.test';
const GROUPED = '7K2M-QX9D-H4TB-R8NW-C3VF-J6PZ-A1GE-Y5KS-M0QT-B7XH-W2DN-F9RC-P4ZA';
const noop = () => {};
const blocked = { 'aria-disabled': true } as const;

function Step({ n, title, footer, children }: { n: number; title: string; footer: ReactNode; children: ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <form noValidate onSubmit={e => e.preventDefault()}>
      <OnboardingFrame title={title} stepLabel={t('signin.step', { n })} footer={footer}>{children}</OnboardingFrame>
    </form>
  );
}
function Login({ refused }: { refused?: boolean }) {
  const [username, setUsername] = useState(refused ? 'ada' : '');
  const [password, setPassword] = useState(refused ? 'hunter22' : '');
  return (
    <Step n={1} title={t('signin.login.title', { instance })}
      footer={<><Button variant="ghost" type="button">{t('signin.login.createInstead')}</Button><Button variant="accent" type="submit">{t('signin.login.submit')}</Button></>}>
      <p>{t('signin.login.body', { instance })}</p>
      <TextField id="s-username" label={t('signin.login.username')} value={username} onChange={setUsername} autoComplete="username" spellCheck={false} />
      <TextField id="s-password" type="password" label={t('signin.login.password')} value={password} onChange={setPassword}
        autoComplete="current-password" error={refused ? t('signin.error.loginFailed') : undefined} />
    </Step>
  );
}
function Key({ value, error, working }: { value: string; error?: string; working?: boolean }) {
  const [text, setText] = useState(value);
  const n = text.replace(/[\s\-–—]/g, '').length;
  const short = n !== 52;
  return (
    <Step n={3} title={t('signin.key.title')}
      footer={<><Button variant="ghost" type="button" {...(working ? blocked : {})}>{t('signin.cancel')}</Button>
        <Button variant="accent" type="submit" {...(short || working ? blocked : {})} aria-describedby={short ? 's-key-length' : undefined}>{t('signin.key.submit')}</Button></>}>
      <p>{t('signin.key.body')}</p>
      <RecoveryKeyField id="s-key" label={t('signin.key.label')} value={text} onChange={setText} hint={t('signin.key.hint', { n })} error={error} />
      {short ? <p id="s-key-length">{t('signin.error.keyLength')}</p> : null}
      {working ? <p role="status">{t('signin.key.working')}</p> : null}
    </Step>
  );
}

export const Login_: Story = { name: 'Login', render: () => <Login /> };
export const LoginRefused: Story = { render: () => <Login refused /> };
export const SecondFactor: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <Step n={2} title={t('signin.totp.title')}
      footer={<><Button variant="ghost" type="button">{t('signin.cancel')}</Button><Button variant="accent" type="submit">{t('signin.login.submit')}</Button></>}>
      <p>{t('signin.totp.body')}</p>
      <TextField id="s-code" label={t('signin.totp.code')} value="" onChange={noop} inputMode="numeric" autoComplete="one-time-code" maxLength={6} />
    </Step>
  ),
};
export const RecoveryKey: Story = { render: () => <Key value={GROUPED.slice(0, 29)} /> };
export const RecoveryKeyWrong: Story = { render: () => <Key value={GROUPED.replace('7K2M', '7K2N')} error={t('signin.error.wrongKey')} /> };
export const NoBackup: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <OnboardingFrame title={t('signin.key.title')} stepLabel={t('signin.step', { n: 3 })} footer={<Button variant="ghost" type="button">{t('signin.cancel')}</Button>}>
      <Banner tone="danger">{t('signin.error.noBackup', { instance })}</Banner>
    </OnboardingFrame>
  ),
};
export const Adding: Story = { render: () => <Key value={GROUPED} working /> };
export const Done: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <OnboardingFrame title={t('signin.done.title')} stepLabel={t('signin.step', { n: 4 })}
      footer={<Button variant="accent" type="button">{t('signin.done.next')}</Button>}>
      <p>{t('signin.done.body', { username: 'ada', instance })}</p>
    </OnboardingFrame>
  ),
};
```

Create `packages/web/src/test/fake-idb.ts` (test support; the IndexedDB subset `prefs.ts` uses, with the real
API's asynchrony, after `packages/client-core/src/account/kek.test.ts:12-122`):

```ts
type Handler = ((event: unknown) => void) | null;

class FakeRequest {
  result: unknown = undefined;
  error: DOMException | null = null;
  onsuccess: Handler = null;
  onerror: Handler = null;
  onupgradeneeded: Handler = null;
  onblocked: Handler = null;
}

class FakeTransaction {
  oncomplete: Handler = null;
  onerror: Handler = null;
  onabort: Handler = null;
  error: DOMException | null = null;
  private pending = 0;
  constructor(private readonly idb: FakeIdb, readonly mode: IDBTransactionMode) {}
  objectStore(name: string): { get(key: string): FakeRequest; put(value: unknown, key: string): FakeRequest } {
    const records = this.idb.stores.get(name);
    if (records === undefined) throw new DOMException(`no object store ${name}`, 'NotFoundError');
    return {
      get: (key: string) => this.run(() => records.get(key)),
      put: (value: unknown, key: string) => {
        if (this.mode !== 'readwrite') throw new DOMException('the transaction is read-only', 'ReadOnlyError');
        return this.run(() => { records.set(key, structuredClone(value)); return key; });
      },
    };
  }
  private run(op: () => unknown): FakeRequest {
    const request = new FakeRequest();
    this.pending += 1;
    queueMicrotask(() => {
      request.result = op();
      request.onsuccess?.({ target: request });
      this.pending -= 1;
      if (this.pending === 0) queueMicrotask(() => this.oncomplete?.({ target: this }));
    });
    return request;
  }
}

/** One in-memory IndexedDB. `failOpen` makes every open fail; `hang` makes it never answer. */
export class FakeIdb {
  readonly stores = new Map<string, Map<string, unknown>>();
  readonly opened: { name: string; version: number }[] = [];
  failOpen = false;
  hang = false;
  private version = 0;
  open(name: string, version: number): FakeRequest {
    const request = new FakeRequest();
    queueMicrotask(() => {
      this.opened.push({ name, version });
      if (this.hang) return;
      if (this.failOpen) {
        request.error = new DOMException('the open failed', 'UnknownError');
        request.onerror?.({ target: request });
        return;
      }
      let upgrading = false;
      request.result = {
        objectStoreNames: { contains: (n: string) => this.stores.has(n) },
        createObjectStore: (n: string) => {
          if (!upgrading) throw new DOMException('not in a version change', 'InvalidStateError');
          this.stores.set(n, new Map());
          return {};
        },
        transaction: (_n: string, mode: IDBTransactionMode = 'readonly') => new FakeTransaction(this, mode),
        close: () => {},
      };
      if (version > this.version) {
        this.version = version;
        upgrading = true;
        request.onupgradeneeded?.({ target: request });
        upgrading = false;
      }
      request.onsuccess?.({ target: request });
    });
    return request;
  }
  get factory(): IDBFactory {
    return this as unknown as IDBFactory;
  }
}
```
